> **Provenance**: Harvested from [syntax-tree/mdast](https://github.com/syntax-tree/mdast) (Revision: `c034ec9d`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When architecting an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), node schemas MUST be partitioned into orthogonal, hierarchical content models (`Flow`, `Phrasing`, `Root`), and parent-child relations MUST enforce strict directional containment: Flow containers MAY contain Flow or Phrasing, but Phrasing nodes MUST NEVER permit Flow children. Recursive transparent constraints MUST NOT attempt to restrict semantic nesting if the underlying source grammar allows it.

**WHY**:
Attempting to enforce negative semantic constraints (e.g., "links cannot contain links") at the static AST type layer using artificial categories like `StaticPhrasingContent` breaks down when the host language grammar (such as CommonMark autolinks embedded in reference links: `[a <http://b> c](d)`) allows the construction. This causes the parser to either crash, emit invalid structural types, or diverge from standard spec compliance.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply when defining any AST, intermediate representation (IR), or document schema in parsers, compilers, formatters, and transformation pipelines across TypeScript, Rust, Go, or Python.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
// Production-grade TypeScript AST Content Model Invariants

// 1. Primitive Unist Interfaces
export interface Point {
  line: number;
  column: number;
  offset?: number;
}

export interface Position {
  start: Point;
  end: Point;
  indent?: number[];
}

export interface Node {
  type: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
  position?: Position;
}

export interface Literal extends Node {
  value: string;
}

export interface Parent extends Node {
  children: MdastContent[];
}

// 2. Strict Content Model Partitioning
export type FlowContent =
  | Blockquote
  | Code
  | Heading
  | HTML
  | List
  | Paragraph
  | Table
  | ThematicBreak;

export type PhrasingContent =
  | Break
  | Delete
  | Emphasis
  | FootnoteReference
  | HTML
  | Image
  | ImageReference
  | InlineCode
  | Link
  | LinkReference
  | Strong
  | Text;

export type ListContent = ListItem;

export type MdastContent = FlowContent | PhrasingContent | ListContent;

// 3. Parent Node Contracts Enforcing Strict Hierarchies
export interface Root extends Parent {
  type: 'root';
  children: FlowContent[];
}

export interface Paragraph extends Parent {
  type: 'paragraph';
  children: PhrasingContent[]; // Flow content strictly forbidden inside Paragraph
}

export interface Blockquote extends Parent {
  type: 'blockquote';
  children: FlowContent[]; // Transparently wraps recursive Flow blocks
}

export interface Link extends Parent {
  type: 'link';
  url: string;
  title?: string | null;
  // CommonMark permits phrasing inside links, even if HTML forbids nested <a> tags.
  // AST mirrors grammar, leaving semantic sanitation to downstream renderers.
  children: PhrasingContent[];
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Artificial type bifurcation attempting to prohibit nested links
// in the AST specification layer.
export type StaticPhrasingContent = Exclude<PhrasingContent, Link | LinkReference>;

export interface EmphasisBroken extends Parent {
  type: 'emphasis';
  // Attempting to enforce that emphasis inside a link cannot contain another link:
  children: StaticPhrasingContent[]; // BREAKS on valid Markdown like: *[foo](url)*
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Implement a compile-time and runtime type assertion suite verifying that valid CommonMark AST permutations satisfy structural type guards:
```typescript
import { assert } from 'node:assert';

function assertValidPhrasing(nodes: Node[]): asserts nodes is PhrasingContent[] {
  const phrasingTypes = new Set([
    'text', 'emphasis', 'strong', 'delete', 'inlineCode', 
    'break', 'link', 'image', 'linkReference', 'imageReference', 'html'
  ]);
  for (const node of nodes) {
    assert(
      phrasingTypes.has(node.type), 
      `Invariant violation: Node type "${node.type}" is not valid PhrasingContent`
    );
  }
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [syntax-tree/mdast](https://github.com/syntax-tree/mdast) (Revision: `c034ec9d`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
An Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) node schema MUST NOT store syntactic delimiter variations, punctuation tokens, or styling characters (such as markdown bullet symbols `*`, `-`, `+` or emphasis delimiters `*` vs `_`). All stylistic and formatting nuances MUST be reconstructed either through positional coordinate lookups against the raw source buffer (`VFile`) or delegated to serializer configuration profiles.

**WHY**:
Polluting AST nodes with concrete syntax metadata (CST properties like `node.delimiter = '*'`) explodes the state space, breaks node interchangeability between different compiler toolchains, violates the single-responsibility principle of AST nodes, and causes AST transform plugins to emit corrupted, nonsensical syntax when mutating or synthesizing new nodes.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
When designing syntax trees, domain-specific language (DSL) representations, query compilers, or serialization/deserialization frameworks.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
// Correct: AST node retains semantic invariants; formatting is externalized

export interface Emphasis extends Parent {
  type: 'emphasis';
  children: PhrasingContent[];
  // Delimiter character ('*' or '_') is deliberately omitted from AST
}

export interface List extends Parent {
  type: 'list';
  ordered?: boolean | null;
  start?: number | null;
  spread?: boolean | null;
  children: ListContent[];
  // Bullet character ('-', '+', '*') is NOT stored here
}

// Accessing original concrete syntax MUST use positional lookups:
export function getConcreteDelimiter(node: Node, sourceBuffer: string): string | null {
  if (!node.position) return null;
  const startOffset = node.position.start.offset;
  if (startOffset === undefined || startOffset >= sourceBuffer.length) {
    return null;
  }
  // Extract concrete token directly from slice without AST mutation
  return sourceBuffer.charAt(startOffset);
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Polluting AST with lexical delimiter artifacts
export interface PollutedEmphasis extends Parent {
  type: 'emphasis';
  character: '*' | '_'; // LEAKS concrete syntax into abstract structural tree
  children: PhrasingContent[];
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Enforce AST purity via schema property verification in test suites:
```typescript
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

test('AST nodes must not contain concrete formatting tokens', () => {
  const allowedKeys = new Set(['type', 'children', 'value', 'position', 'data', 'url', 'title', 'alt', 'lang', 'meta', 'ordered', 'start', 'spread', 'depth']);
  
  function verifyNodeKeys(node: Record<string, unknown>) {
    for (const key of Object.keys(node)) {
      assert(
        allowedKeys.has(key), 
        `Forbidden concrete syntax key "${key}" detected on node type "${node.type}"`
      );
    }
    if (Array.isArray(node.children)) {
      for (const child of node.children) verifyNodeKeys(child as Record<string, unknown>);
    }
  }
});
```

**RULE**:
When an open-source architecture decouples its formal specification from its runtime implementation packages, the specification repository MUST set `"private": true` or explicitly publish a deprecated placeholder stub on package registries. PROVENANCE_END -->
> **Provenance**: Harvested from [fastapi/fastapi](https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi) (Revision: `b23d78f2`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When adapting a synchronous Python context manager into an asynchronous context manager (`@asynccontextmanager`) backed by a worker threadpool, `cm.__exit__` MUST execute with an isolated, dedicated capacity limiter (or unconstrained limiter), rather than borrowing or competing for the global/shared threadpool capacity limiter used by `cm.__enter__`.

**WHY**:
If `cm.__enter__` acquires a shared resource (such as a database connection from a bounded pool) on a shared threadpool, and the event loop saturates the shared threadpool with subsequent `cm.__enter__` tasks, the system enters an unrecoverable deadlock (Resource Acquisition At Degradation Starvation). The thread pool is exhausted by tasks waiting for connections, while the tasks holding connections cannot run `cm.__exit__` because the thread pool has no free worker slots. Supplying an isolated `CapacityLimiter(1)` solely for `cm.__exit__` guarantees that release/cleanup operations are never starved by inbound acquisition tasks.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any asynchronous runtime (AnyIO, asyncio, Trio, Twisted) bridging synchronous context managers (SQLAlchemy sessions, psycopg2 connections, Redis connections, disk file handles) into async generator lifecycles.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import AbstractContextManager, asynccontextmanager
from typing import TypeVar
import anyio.to_thread
from anyio import CapacityLimiter
from starlette.concurrency import run_in_threadpool

_T = TypeVar("_T")

@asynccontextmanager
async def contextmanager_in_threadpool(
    cm: AbstractContextManager[_T],
) -> AsyncGenerator[_T, None]:
    # A dedicated limiter for __exit__ ensures that teardown never starves
    # if the main worker pool is saturated with inbound requests.
    exit_limiter = CapacityLimiter(1)
    try:
        # Run __enter__ on the shared threadpool
        yield await run_in_threadpool(cm.__enter__)
    except Exception as e:
        ok = bool(
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(
                cm.__exit__, type(e), e, e.__traceback__, limiter=exit_limiter
            )
        )
        if not ok:
            raise e
    else:
        await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(
            cm.__exit__, None, None, None, limiter=exit_limiter
        )
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```python
# ANTI-PATTERN: Reusing the default threadpool for cm.__exit__
@asynccontextmanager
async def leaky_contextmanager(cm):
    try:
        # If threadpool has N slots, and N concurrent requests enter here:
        yield await run_in_threadpool(cm.__enter__)
    finally:
        # DEADLOCK: Threadpool capacity is 0, __exit__ is queued indefinitely.
        # Connections in the pool are never released, freezing the server process.
        await run_in_threadpool(cm.__exit__, None, None, None)
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Run an integration test with a pool size equal to the threadpool worker limit ($N$), initiate $N$ concurrent requests, throw an exception inside the yielded block, and verify that all $N$ context managers complete `__exit__` within a strict timeout ($< 1.0\text{s}$) rather than timing out or hanging indefinitely.

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [fastapi/fastapi](https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi) (Revision: `b23d78f2`).

**RULE**:
Before piping deserialized or arbitrary Python objects into standard JSON lines (`JSONL`) or Server-Sent Events (`SSE`) streaming buffers that utilize standard `json.dumps`, the serialization layer MUST recursively normalize non-finite IEEE 754 floating-point values (`math.nan`, `math.inf`, `-math.inf`) to JSON-compliant `None` (or configured string representations), while preserving non-string dictionary keys and primitive scalar values.

**WHY**:
JavaScript Object Notation (RFC 8259 § 6) explicitly forbids `NaN`, `Infinity`, and `-Infinity`. Python's native `json.dumps()` allows these values by default (`allow_nan=True`), emitting JavaScript-incompatible tokens: `{"val": NaN}`. When consumed by frontend parsers (`JSON.parse` in browsers or Node.js), parsing fails with a fatal `SyntaxError: Unexpected token N in JSON at position X`. While Pydantic v2 handles this at the model level via `model_dump_json()`, raw dictionaries, untyped generators, or Server-Sent Events wrapping unstructured payloads bypass Pydantic model serialization and crash client-side streaming consumers unless sanitized.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any HTTP streaming route, SSE emitter (`EventSourceResponse`), JSONL ndjson line-delimited stream, or websocket pipeline yielding dynamically constructed dictionaries or primitive floats to HTTP clients.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
import math
from typing import Any

def normalize_non_finite_floats(data: Any) -> Any:
    """
    Recursively replaces non-finite float values in JSON-compatible structures
    with None, preserving dict keys, non-float primitives, and nested structures.
    """
    if isinstance(data, float):
        return data if math.isfinite(data) else None
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        return {
            key: normalize_non_finite_floats(value) 
            for key, value in data.items()
        }
    if isinstance(data, list):
        return [normalize_non_finite_floats(value) for value in data]
    return data
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```python
# ANTI-PATTERN: Serializing raw generator items directly to stream bytes
async def event_generator():
    yield {"ratio": float("nan"), "status": "running"}

async def bad_sse_endpoint():
    async for item in event_generator():
        # Emits: b'data: {"ratio": NaN, "status": "running"}\n\n'
        # Crashes `JSON.parse()` in the browser with SyntaxError!
        yield f"data: {json.dumps(item)}\n\n".encode("utf-8")
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Parameterized unit test verifying that emitting `[float("nan"), float("inf"), float("-inf"), {"nested": [float("nan")]}]` through an SSE or JSONL response pipeline deserializes via a strict RFC-compliant JSON parser (`json.loads` without non-standard extensions) into `[None, None, None, {"nested": [None]}]`.

**RULE**:
When wrapping or mounting Starlette routers (`Route`, `WebSocketRoute`, `Mount`, `Host`) inside an application router abstraction that produces route inspection metadata (`iter_route_contexts()`), the introspection traversal MUST check if the contextual wrapper contains a direct underlying `.starlette_route`. **WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply when implementing API routing layers, gateway adapters, or OpenAPI schema generation tools that wrap or nest underlying ASGI framework routes.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
from starlette.routing import BaseRoute

class RouteContextWrapper:
    def __init__(self, route: BaseRoute, route_context: Any | None = None) -> None:
        self.route = route
        self._route_context = route_context

    @property
    def original_route(self) -> BaseRoute:
        return self.route

    @property
    def _effective_route(self) -> BaseRoute:
        if self._route_context is not None:
            # Crucial invariant: if an inner starlette_route exists in context,
            # surface it to preserve route metadata, path convertors, and methods.
            if getattr(self._route_context, "starlette_route", None) is not None:
                return self._route_context.starlette_route
            return self._route_context
        return self.route
```

**RULE**:
Network endpoint host/port extraction from user configuration, request headers, or authority strings MUST NEVER use single-character delimiter splitting (e.g., `str.partition(":")`, `str.split(":")`, or regex `^([^:]+):(\d+)$`). Network parsing MUST parse the authority segment using an RFC 3986/RFC 5952 compliant URI parser (e.g., `urllib.parse.urlsplit("//" + authority)`).

**WHY**:
IPv6 literal addresses contain multiple colons (e.g., `[::1]:8080`, `[2001:db8::1]`). Splitting on the first colon yields an invalid host token `[` and invalid port `::1]:8080`. Splitting on the last colon fails on bare IPv6 addresses without ports (`[::1]`). This corrupts socket binding, test client session resolution, cookie domain scoping, and SNI headers, inducing critical networking faults.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any networking, web, proxy, or microservice infrastructure codebase that consumes socket configurations, `Host` HTTP headers, upstream proxy targets, or URI authorities in Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or C++.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
import collections.abc as cabc
from urllib.parse import urlsplit


def extract_host_port(
    authority: str, default_port: int = 5000
) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Extract host and port safely supporting IPv4, IPv6 literals, and hostnames.

    Authority string is normalized as a schemeless network location using '//'.
    """
    if not authority:
        return "127.0.0.1", default_port

    parsed = urlsplit(f"//{authority}")
    host = parsed.hostname or "127.0.0.1"
    port = parsed.port if parsed.port is not None else default_port

    # Strip potential outer square brackets if raw IP is needed for socket bind
    return host, port
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```python
def extract_host_port_unsafe(
    authority: str, default_port: int = 5000
) -> tuple[str, int]:
    # CRITICAL BUG: Fails violently when authority is an IPv6 literal (e.g. "[::1]:8080")
    host, _, port_str = authority.partition(":")
    # host becomes "[" and port_str becomes ":1]:8080"
    port = int(port_str) if port_str else default_port
    return host, port
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Enforce unit/property tests parameterizing IPv6 loopback, link-local, and public addresses:

```python
import pytest


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_addr", "expected_host", "expected_port"),
    [
        ("localhost:8080", "localhost", 8080),
        ("127.0.0.1:443", "127.0.0.1", 443),
        ("[::1]:8000", "::1", 8000),
        ("[::1]", "::1", 5000),
        ("[fe80::1ff:fe23:4567:890a]:9000", "fe80::1ff:fe23:4567:890a", 9000),
    ],
)
def test_extract_host_port_invariants(input_addr, expected_host, expected_port):
    host, port = extract_host_port(input_addr, default_port=5000)
    assert host == expected_host
    assert port == expected_port
```

**RULE**:
When an operational flag can be configured at multiple levels (Global Config -> Decorator / Routing Spec -> View Class/Function Attribute), default fallback logic MUST NOT use truthiness evaluation (`if not flag:`) or blind boolean overriding. Handlers MUST evaluate values against an explicit sentinel (such as `None`) through strict precedence cascades.

**WHY**:
Evaluating boolean feature toggles using `if flag:` or coalescing with `flag or config_default` prevents callers from explicitly disabling a feature (`flag = False`) when the global configuration defaults to `True`. Conversely, it prevents locally enabling a feature (`flag = True`) if the intermediate fallback logic re-asserts an upstream falsy condition.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Configuration resolution in routing systems, CLI option resolution, database connection pooling parameters, and plugin feature gates where flags default to `None` (inherit) but accept explicit `True` or `False`.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any


def resolve_automatic_options(
    rule_level_flag: bool | None,
    view_func: Callable[..., Any],
    global_config: dict[str, Any],
    methods: set[str],
) -> bool:
    """Resolve automatic OPTIONS generation respecting 3-tier precedence:

    1. Explicit rule/route argument
    2. Explicit view-function attribute
    3. Global application configuration
    """
    provide_automatic_options = rule_level_flag

    # Tier 2: Check function attribute if route level was unasserted (None)
    if provide_automatic_options is None:
        provide_automatic_options = getattr(
            view_func, "provide_automatic_options", None
        )

    # Tier 3: Check global application config if function attribute was unasserted
    if provide_automatic_options is None:
        provide_automatic_options = (
            "OPTIONS" not in methods
            and global_config.get("PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS", True)
        )

    return bool(provide_automatic_options)
```

**RULE**:
When an error pipeline exposes a mechanism to map an `err.statusCode` or `err.status` directly to an HTTP response status code, the engine MUST enforce that the value is an integer strictly bounded within `[400, 599]`. If the assigned property falls outside this inclusive range (e.g., `< 400`, `>= 600`), or is not an integer, the runtime MUST deterministically fall back to `500 Internal Server Error`.

**WHY**:
Allowing arbitrary numeric codes (such as `200`, `302`, or invalid protocol numbers like `600` or `999`) on error objects violates RFC 9110 HTTP semantics and destabilizes downstream observability, reverse proxies, and tracing diagnostic channels (e.g., OpenTelemetry, `node:diagnostics_channel`). Furthermore, Node's native HTTP parser crashes or throws `ERR_HTTP_INVALID_STATUS_CODE` when an invalid range is dispatched to `res.writeHead()`, turning a handled application error into an unhandled socket drop.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in all API gateways, web framework response handlers, RPC-to-HTTP translators, and error-handling middleware across any language runtime before dispatching to the transport socket.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// lib/error-status.js & lib/error-handler.js pattern
const kReplyHasStatusCode = Symbol('fastify.reply.hasStatusCode')

function determineValidStatusCode (err, fallback = 500) {
  if (typeof err !== 'object' || err === null) {
    return fallback
  }

  // Priority order: statusCode over status
  const code = err.statusCode ?? err.status

  if (typeof code === 'number' && Number.isInteger(code) && code >= 400 && code <= 599) {
    return code
  }

  return fallback
}

function setErrorStatusCode (reply, err) {
  // If user explicitly called reply.code(...) with a non-200, retain it
  if (!reply[kReplyHasStatusCode] || reply.statusCode === 200) {
    const finalCode = determineValidStatusCode(err, 500)
    reply.code(finalCode)
  }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// NEVER allow arbitrary error status codes to pass through unchecked
function unsafeSetErrorStatusCode (reply, err) {
  // ANTI-PATTERN: Truthy check or single lower-bound check allows status: 200, 600, 9999
  const statusCode = err && (err.statusCode || err.status)
  reply.code(statusCode >= 400 ? statusCode : 500) // FAILS: err.statusCode = 600 crashes HTTP parser!
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
```javascript
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'

test('deterministic error status clamping across invalid domains', () => {
  const testCases = [
    { err: { statusCode: 200 }, expected: 500 },
    { err: { statusCode: 302 }, expected: 500 },
    { err: { statusCode: 600 }, expected: 500 },
    { err: { statusCode: 999 }, expected: 500 },
    { err: { statusCode: NaN }, expected: 500 },
    { err: { statusCode: 404 }, expected: 404 },
    { err: { status: 503 }, expected: 503 },
    { err: { statusCode: 418, status: 500 }, expected: 418 } // Priority verification
  ]

  for (const { err, expected } of testCases) {
    assert.strictEqual(determineValidStatusCode(err), expected)
  }
})
```

**RULE**:
When setting or appending to HTTP response headers that support multi-value accumulation via arrays (specifically `Set-Cookie`), the target frame MUST defensively clone any array supplied by the caller before storing or mutating it. The framework MUST NOT directly reference or mutate the input array instance.

**WHY**:
In Node.js web architectures, developers frequently define static base configurations or cookie options at the module scope (e.g., `const DEFAULT_COOKIES = ['sessionId=...']`). If a reply handler stores this array directly and subsequent calls execute `this.headers['set-cookie'].push(...)`, the shared module-level array is mutated in place. Across successive HTTP requests, this causes memory leaks and cross-request state pollution, repeatedly duplicating set-cookie entries across distinct client sessions.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any HTTP context where multi-value headers (`Set-Cookie`, `Warning`, `Link`) are represented as arrays and manipulated across asynchronous lifecycles.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// lib/reply.js header storage invariant
Reply.prototype.header = function (key, value = '') {
  const normalizedKey = key.toLowerCase()

  if (this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey] !== undefined) {
    if (normalizedKey === 'set-cookie') {
      // If already tracking, convert/append safely
      if (Array.isArray(this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey])) {
        if (Array.isArray(value)) {
          this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey].push(...value)
        } else {
          this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey].push(value)
        }
      } else {
        this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey] = [this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey], value]
      }
    } else {
      this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey] = value
    }
  } else if (normalizedKey === 'set-cookie' && Array.isArray(value)) {
    // CRITICAL: Defensive copy protects module-level constants from in-place push mutations
    this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey] = value.slice()
  } else {
    this[kReplyHeaders][normalizedKey] = value
  }

  return this
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// NEVER assign an external array reference directly if downstream functions mutate it
Reply.prototype.unsafeHeader = function (key, value) {
  // ANTI-PATTERN: Stores caller's array directly. A subsequent .push() leaks across requests!
  this[kReplyHeaders][key.toLowerCase()] = value
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
```javascript
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'

test('header array registration does not mutate caller array instance', () => {
  const sharedCookieConfig = Object.freeze(['auth=token']) // Freezing proves mutation prevention
  const replyMock = { [kReplyHeaders]: {} }

  // Must not throw TypeError: Cannot add property ... of object #<Object> is not extensible
  // when cloning with .slice()
  const copied = sharedCookieConfig.slice()
  replyMock[kReplyHeaders]['set-cookie'] = copied
  replyMock[kReplyHeaders]['set-cookie'].push('theme=dark')

  assert.strictEqual(sharedCookieConfig.length, 1)
  assert.strictEqual(replyMock[kReplyHeaders]['set-cookie'].length, 2)
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [fastify/fastify](https://github.com/fastify/fastify) (Revision: `e03b48ba`).

**RULE**:
An asynchronous schema validation compiler that resolves via a Promise MUST only communicate binary validation success or failure (or throw an explicit error). The validation engine MUST NOT unwrap an asynchronously resolved object shape containing `{ value, error }` to override request inputs or declare failures.

**WHY**:
In synchronous validator adapters (such as Joi or standard Ajv compilers), returning an object shaped as `{ value, error }` allows in-place property coercion and synchronous error propagation. However, in an asynchronous validator (such as Ajv with `$async: true`), the promise resolves with the validated data payload itself. If an async pipeline attempts to unwrap `{ value, error }` from the resolved promise, an attacker can transmit an HTTP payload containing a root property named `"error"` or `"value"` (e.g., `{"error": "Exploit"}` or `{"value": {"injected": "payload"}}`). This collapses the pipeline into an unintended validation failure or allows the request body to be substituted with untrusted arbitrary data.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to all validation pipelines, RPC payload validators, and input processing engines supporting hybrid synchronous/asynchronous schema execution.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// lib/validation.js invariant
function validateParam (validatorFunction, request, paramName) {
  let ret

  try {
    ret = validatorFunction(request[paramName])
  } catch (err) {
    return err // Synchronous throw is an immediate failure
  }

  // Handle Async Validator (Promise-based, e.g., $async Ajv)
  if (ret && typeof ret.then === 'function') {
    return ret
      .then((res) => {
        // MUST NOT unwrap { value, error } here.
        // A resolved promise is a pass unless strictly evaluated as false.
        // The resolved object IS the validated payload.
        return res === false ? validatorFunction.errors : false
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        // Async failure MUST be signaled via promise rejection
        return err
      })
  }

  // Synchronous Validator Contract: { value, error } unwrapping is ONLY allowed here
  if (ret != null && typeof ret === 'object') {
    if (ret.error) return ret.error
    if ('value' in ret) request[paramName] = ret.value
    return false
  }

  return ret === false ? validatorFunction.errors : false
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// NEVER pass async resolved values into polymorphic unwrappers
function unsafeAsyncValidation (ret) {
  return ret.then((res) => {
    // ANTI-PATTERN: Unwrapping 'res' allows a JSON body like {"value": "hacked"}
    // to overwrite the body or {"error": "boom"} to trigger an arbitrary validation failure!
    if (res && res.error) return res.error
    if (res && res.value) return res.value
    return false
  })
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
```javascript
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'

test('async validation with payload containing "value" or "error" keys must not alter execution', async () => {
  const asyncSchemaValidator = async (data) => {
    // Resolves with data as per $async AJV spec
    return data
  }

  const mockRequest = {
    body: { hello: 'world', value: { malicious: true }, error: 'fake error' }
  }

  const result = await validateParam(asyncSchemaValidator, mockRequest, 'body')

  // Validation must pass without errors
  assert.strictEqual(result, false)
  // Request body must remain identical and not replaced by mockRequest.body.value
  assert.strictEqual(mockRequest.body.hello, 'world')
  assert.strictEqual(mockRequest.body.value.malicious, true)
})
```

**RULE**:
When designing long-running autonomous worker pools, batch harvesting pipelines, or self-evolving AI architectures:
1. **Dead-Letter Poison-Pill Quarantine**: Any job target that returns an unrecoverable terminal error (e.g. `HTTP 404 Not Found`, permanently deleted account, revoked token, corrupt data schema) MUST immediately be written to a persistent registry with a terminal status (e.g., `DEAD_OR_UNAVAILABLE` or `404_OR_UNAVAILABLE`). Target selectors MUST explicitly exclude quarantined entries so that workers NEVER attempt endless re-executions on non-existent resources.
2. **Self-Referential Meta-Learning Loop**: The intelligence engine MUST treat its own repository, configuration, and factory workflows as a tier-1 learning source. All bug fixes, incident autopsies, and architectural refactorings committed to the engine itself MUST be distilled into a dedicated learning dossier (`07_PROJECT_LEARNING/ai-builder-brain-learnings.md`) and promoted into universal knowledge rules.
3. **Atomic Rebase-Retry Concurrency**: Autonomous background workers pushing state to a shared remote Git ledger MUST execute inside an exponential-backoff retry loop with automatic rebase (`git pull --rebase origin main`) and index lock purging (`rm -f .git/index.lock`), ensuring zero runner discoveries are discarded due to concurrent pushes.

**WHY**:
Prevents catastrophic worker starvation observed in Incident `INC-002`: when unrecoverable targets fail without persistent status flags, queues re-feed the exact same failing targets to every worker on every cycle. This causes the fleet to report continuous green execution while generating 0 bytes of meaningful work. Furthermore, without self-referential meta-learning, an AI system remains blind to its own past bugs and repeats solved architectural blunders.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Distributed crawler swarms, message queue consumers (BullMQ, Celery, SQS), background scraping daemons, and autonomous agent systems that modify their own codebases.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// queue/target-selector.js
export function selectNextHarvestTarget(queue, sourcesRegistry, assignedSet = new Set()) {
  for (const item of queue) {
    if (assignedSet.has(item.slug)) continue;

    const entry = sourcesRegistry[item.slug];
    
    // 1. Poison-Pill Quarantine Guard: Never pick dead or terminal 404 targets
    if (entry && (entry.harvestStatus === '404_OR_UNAVAILABLE' || entry.harvestStatus === 'DEAD_OR_UNAVAILABLE')) {
      continue;
    }

    // 2. Select only genuinely unharvested or healthy rotation items
    if (!entry || entry.harvestStatus === 'PENDING') {
      assignedSet.add(item.slug);
      return item;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:

```javascript
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [expressjs/express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) (Revision: `0dee2c52`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When generating HTTP response headers, transport-level framing headers (`Transfer-Encoding`) and length-delimiting headers (`Content-Length`) MUST be treated as strictly mutually exclusive per RFC 9112 Section 6.1. However, payload inspection logic (such as calculating buffer byte length, hashing payload slices, and deriving ETags) MUST execute independently of whether `Transfer-Encoding` is present. Never nest payload metadata derivation inside a `!res.hasHeader('Transfer-Encoding')` conditional block.

**WHY**:
Nesting length calculation and hash derivation inside a check that guards against emitting `Content-Length` causes silent omission of caching validators (such as `ETag`). When an upstream proxy or middleware sets `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, downstream conditional caching (`304 Not Modified`, `If-None-Match`) breaks silently because the entity tag calculation was erroneously aborted alongside the `Content-Length` header assignment.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any web framework, reverse proxy, or HTTP response serializer handling buffer or string bodies where chunked streaming and cache validation headers coexist.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// Verified production-grade implementation from Express res.send logic (lib/response.js)
function finalizeResponsePayload(res, app, chunk, encoding) {
  var len;

  // 1. Calculate payload byte length unconditionally for metadata derivation
  if (chunk !== undefined) {
    if (Buffer.isBuffer(chunk)) {
      len = chunk.length;
    } else if (typeof chunk === 'string') {
      len = Buffer.byteLength(chunk, encoding);
    } else {
      // JSON or primitive type normalized to string buffer prior to entry
      len = Buffer.byteLength(chunk, encoding);
    }

    // 2. Conditionally assign Content-Length ONLY if Transfer-Encoding is absent.
    // RFC 9112: A sender MUST NOT send a Content-Length header field in any message
    // that contains a Transfer-Encoding header field.
    if (!res.get('Transfer-Encoding')) {
      res.set('Content-Length', len);
    }
  }

  // 3. ETag generation depends on payload content and calculated length, NOT transport framing
  var etagFn = app.get('etag fn');
  var generateETag = !res.get('ETag') && typeof etagFn === 'function';

  if (generateETag && len !== undefined) {
    var computedETag = etagFn(chunk, encoding);
    if (computedETag) {
      res.set('ETag', computedETag);
    }
  }

  return chunk;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Coupling payload metadata extraction to header presence
if (chunk !== undefined && !res.get('Transfer-Encoding')) {
  // If Transfer-Encoding was injected upstream (e.g., chunked),
  // this whole block is skipped!
  len = Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk.length : Buffer.byteLength(chunk, encoding);
  res.set('Content-Length', len);
  
  // BUG: ETag generation nested here fails completely when chunked!
  res.set('ETag', etagFn(chunk)); 
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Automated integration test sending a body with an explicit `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header, asserting the complete absence of `Content-Length` and asserting the exact presence of the calculated `ETag`:
```javascript
it('should generate ETag even if Transfer-Encoding is set', function (done) {
  var app = express();
  app.use(function (_, res) {
    res.set('Transfer-Encoding', 'chunked').send('forensic-payload');
  });

  request(app)
    .get('/')
    .expect(200)
    .expect(function (res) {
      if (res.headers['content-length'] !== undefined) {
        throw new Error('Content-Length MUST NOT be set when Transfer-Encoding is present');
      }
      if (!res.headers['etag']) {
        throw new Error('ETag MUST be generated regardless of Transfer-Encoding');
      }
    })
    .end(done);
});
```

**RULE**:
When implementing conditional HTTP caching checks (`req.fresh` evaluation for `If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since`), the validator MUST NOT artificially restrict validation solely to `GET` and `HEAD`. Any safe, idempotent, or query-based method defined by IETF RFCs that permits payload revalidation (specifically including the HTTP `QUERY` method per RFC 10008) MUST be permitted to revalidate against resource state and return `304 Not Modified`.

**WHY**:
The HTTP `QUERY` method enables clients to send complex query parameters within a request payload (avoiding URI length limitations) while maintaining safe and idempotent semantics identical to `GET`. Hardcoding `if (req.method !== 'GET' && req.method !== 'HEAD') return false;` guarantees that `QUERY` responses re-download duplicate bodies over the network, completely invalidating cache revalidation infrastructure and causing bandwidth waste and latency regressions.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to all request-freshness calculators, caching proxies, API gateways, and web frameworks running in environments supporting extended HTTP methods (such as Node.js >= 22 where `http.METHODS` contains `QUERY`).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// Verified production-grade freshness validation (lib/request.js)
function isRequestFresh(req, res) {
  var method = req.method;
  var status = res.statusCode;

  // 1. Authorize only safe/idempotent cache-validation candidate methods
  // Matches RFC 9110 (GET/HEAD) and RFC 10008 (QUERY)
  if (method !== 'GET' && method !== 'HEAD' && method !== 'QUERY') {
    return false;
  }

  // 2. 2xx/304 response code status check
  var is2xx = (status >= 200 && status < 300);
  if (!is2xx && status !== 304) {
    return false;
  }

  // 3. Delegate to fresh validator checking If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since
  return fresh(req.headers, {
    'etag': res.get('ETag'),
    'last-modified': res.get('Last-Modified')
  });
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript

req.fresh = function() {
  // Permanently cripples RFC 10008 QUERY method revalidation
  if (this.method !== 'GET' && this.method !== 'HEAD') {
    return false;
  }
  return fresh(this.headers, {
    'etag': this.res.get('ETag'),
    'last-modified': this.res.get('Last-Modified')
  });
};
```

```javascript
  var app = express();
  app.query('/search', function (req, res) {
    res.set('ETag', '"target-hash-123"').json({ data: [1, 2, 3] });

    .query('/search')
    .set('If-None-Match', '"target-hash-123"')
    .send({ filter: 'all' })
    .expect(304, function (err, res) {
      if (err) return done(err);
      assert.strictEqual(res.text, '');
      done();
```

**RULE**:
When an application or routing engine swaps the prototype chain or alters the context references (`req.__proto__`, `res.__proto__`, `req.app`) of mutable shared objects passing through nested, mounted sub-routers or sub-applications, the execution harness MUST register an unwinding exit hook (or teardown continuation) that restores the exact original prototype chain and app pointers when control yields back via `next()`.

**WHY**:
Failure to restore prototypes upon sub-app `next()` completion leaks the mounted application's prototype and settings (`trust proxy`, custom request helpers, route parsing flags) into subsequent middleware executed by the parent app. This creates critical security vulnerabilities: downstream parent middleware might treat spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` client headers as trusted IP addresses because the sub-app had `app.set('trust proxy', true)`, whereas the parent application explicitly forbade proxy trust.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply whenever designing middleware engines, micro-frontends, or embedded execution pipelines that mutate shared global or request-scoped object prototypes to inject local domain capabilities.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// Production-grade scope preservation and unwinding mechanism
function handleSubApp(subApp, req, res, next) {
  // 1. Snapshot original prototype chain and context references
  var originalReqProto = Object.getPrototypeOf(req);
  var originalResProto = Object.getPrototypeOf(res);
  var originalApp = req.app;
  var originalResApp = res.app;

  // 2. Define safe unwinding continuation
  function restoreAndNext(err) {
    // Unconditionally revert the prototype chains
    Object.setPrototypeOf(req, originalReqProto);
    Object.setPrototypeOf(res, originalResProto);
    
    // Restore direct application pointers
    req.app = originalApp;
    res.app = originalResApp;

    // Yield control back to parent stack
    next(err);
  }

  // 3. Inject sub-app prototype context
  Object.setPrototypeOf(req, subApp.request);
  Object.setPrototypeOf(res, subApp.response);
  req.app = subApp;
  res.app = subApp;

  // 4. Delegate to sub-app router with unwinding callback
  subApp.handle(req, res, restoreAndNext);
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// ANTI-PATTERN: One-way prototype mutation without unwinding
function unsafeSubAppHandle(subApp, req, res, next) {
  // Prototype is mutated in-place
  req.__proto__ = subApp.request;
  res.__proto__ = subApp.response;
  req.app = subApp;

  // If subApp does not finalize the response and calls next(),
  // the parent router continues execution, but req.__proto__ remains subApp.request!
  subApp.handle(req, res, next);
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Construct an integration test mounting a sub-app with conflicting security configurations, verifying prototype restoration after `next()`:
```javascript
it('should restore parent settings after yielding from subApp', function (done) {
  var parent = express();
  var subApp = express();

  parent.set('trust proxy', false);
  subApp.set('trust proxy', true);

  subApp.use(function (req, res, next) {
    next(); // Yield without terminating
  });

  parent.use('/sub', subApp);
  parent.use('/sub', function (req, res) {
    // If bug exists, req.app is subApp and trust proxy is true
    res.json({
      isProxyTrusted: req.app.get('trust proxy'),
      matchesParent: req.app === parent
    });
  });

  request(parent)
    .get('/sub')
    .expect(200, {
      isProxyTrusted: false,
      matchesParent: true
    }, done);
});
```

**WHEN TO APPLY**:

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
import { createDefu } from "defu";
import { mergeHooks } from "hookable";

function isPlainObject(value: unknown): value is Record<PropertyKey, any> {
  return Boolean(value) && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value);
}

export function mergeConfigHooks(
  target: Record<PropertyKey, any>,
  key: PropertyKey,
  sourceValue: any,
  namespace: string
): boolean {
  // Target root-level or namespaced "hooks" objects
  if (key === "hooks" && !namespace && isPlainObject(target.hooks) && isPlainObject(sourceValue)) {
    target.hooks = mergeHooks(target.hooks, sourceValue);
    return true; // Short-circuits defu's default overwrite/merge behavior
  }
  return false;
}

export const mergeNitroConfig = createDefu(mergeConfigHooks) as (...sources: any[]) => any;
```

**WHEN TO APPLY**:

```typescript
export interface ManagedInstance {
  close: () => Promise<void>;
}

export function createManagedInstance(hooks: Hookable<Record<string, any>>): ManagedInstance {
  let closePromise: Promise<void> | undefined;

  const instance: ManagedInstance = {
    // Nullish coalescing assignment guarantees single execution across concurrent calls
    close: () => (closePromise ??= Promise.resolve(hooks.callHook("close"))),
  };

  return instance;
}
```

**RULE**:

**WHY**:
If an edge router rule omits `"continue": true`, it acts as a terminal match. If an engineer attempts to opt-out a sub-path from a broad redirect (`/foo/**` -> `/bar`) by inserting a terminal non-redirect route for `/foo/keep`, the edge engine immediately halts evaluation. This skips all subsequent rules—including static asset resolution (`handle: filesystem`), security headers, and deployment skew-protection tokens—resulting in broken asset delivery and missing headers.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any static or edge deployment compiler translating hierarchical route definitions (with opt-outs or exemptions) into linear regular expression routing tables.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:

```typescript
/**
 * Keeps specific sub-routes out of a parent route regex via negative lookahead,
 * preserving subsequent route evaluation without prematurely halting the router.
 * Named capture groups are stripped to non-capturing groups to preserve regex group index references ($1, $2).
 */
export function excludePathsFromRouteRegex(srcRegex: RegExp, excludedPaths: RegExp[]): string {
  const sanitizedNegativePatterns = excludedPaths.map((path) =>
    path.source
      .slice(1, -1) // Strip leading '^' and trailing '$'
      .replace(/\(\?<(?![=!])[^>]*>/g, "(?:") // Neutralize named capture groups to non-capturing
  );

  if (sanitizedNegativePatterns.length === 0) {
    return srcRegex.source;
  }

  // Inject negative lookahead right after '^'
  return `^(?!(?:${sanitizedNegativePatterns.join("|")})$)${srcRegex.source.slice(1)}`;
}
```

**RULE**:
When transforming, joining, or forwarding dynamic URL paths (such as wildcard routing `/**` or splat captures) into proxy destinations or HTTP redirects, the software MUST NOT rely solely on string concatenation or pre-join lexical sanitization. It MUST resolve the target URL through a spec-compliant URL parser against the authorized destination base, verify that `target.origin === base.origin`, enforce that the resulting pathname begins strictly with the expected base directory prefix, and reject all multi-slash (`//`), backslash (`\\`), or percent-encoded separator sequences (`%2f`, `%5c`, `%252f`) at the segment boundary.

**WHY**:
Dynamic path prefixes and wildcard tails often contain user-controlled input. Pre-join path checks fail because path join operations collapse consecutive empty segments (`/foo//../bar` -> `/bar`) or unmask encoded traversal tokens. If an attacker passes `//evil.example` into a naive base-join routine (`base + tail`), a target intended to be `/prefix//evil.example` transforms into a protocol-relative URL pointing to an external domain (`//evil.example`), resulting in Open Redirect or Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any API gateway, reverse proxy, reverse routing engine, static file handler, or CLI documentation launcher that routes request paths into outbound URLs or OS shell executions.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
import { URL } from "node:url";

export class SecurityTrappingError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "SecurityTrappingError";
  }
}

const LEADING_SEPARATOR_RUN_RE = /^(?:[/\\\\]|%(?:25)*(?:2f|5c))+/i;

export function safeResolveTarget(baseTarget: string, untrustedTail: string): string {
  // 1. Strip leading run of all forward/back slashes and double-encoded variants
  const sanitizedTail = untrustedTail.replace(LEADING_SEPARATOR_RUN_RE, "");
  
  // 2. Normalize base URL to ensure trailing slash invariance
  const baseUri = new URL(baseTarget.endsWith("/") ? baseTarget : `${baseTarget}/`);
  
  // 3. Resolve using URL parser constructor
  const resolved = new URL(sanitizedTail, baseUri);

  // 4. Origin lockdown: strictly prohibit protocol or host shifts
  if (resolved.origin !== baseUri.origin) {
    throw new SecurityTrappingError(`Target origin shift detected: ${resolved.origin} !== ${baseUri.origin}`);
  }

  // 5. Path confinement: confirm resolved path resides strictly inside target base
  const expectedBasePath = baseUri.pathname.endsWith("/") ? baseUri.pathname : `${baseUri.pathname}/`;
  if (!resolved.pathname.startsWith(expectedBasePath) && resolved.pathname !== baseUri.pathname.replace(/\/$/, "")) {
    throw new SecurityTrappingError(`Path breakout detected: ${resolved.pathname} outside ${expectedBasePath}`);
  }

  // 6. Strip userinfo (username/password) and collapse repeated directory separators
  resolved.username = "";
  resolved.password = "";
  resolved.pathname = resolved.pathname.replace(/\/{2,}/g, "/");

  return resolved.href;
}
```

```typescript
    throw new Error("Traversal detected"); // BYPASSED via %2e%2e or unnormalized slashes

}
```

**RULE**:
When an asynchronous response or background task terminates prematurely after sending bytes or headers over the wire, the pipeline MUST propagate a unique, immutable sentinel symbol (e.g., `kHandled`) instead of standard operational errors. Downstream middleware, error-rendering handlers, and framework wrappers MUST check for this sentinel and MUST NOT attempt to serialize, re-render, or append a secondary error response (e.g., JSON 500) if the sentinel is detected.

**WHY**:
In streaming architectures (such as Node.js `.pipe()`, Web Streams, or SSE), headers and partial payloads are committed immediately. If a generator or piped stream fails halfway through transmission, the HTTP status is already fixed (typically 200 OK) and chunks are already in flight. If generic error-handling middleware intercepts this exception and treats it as an unhandled error, it will attempt to mutate response headers and output an error payload (e.g., `{"status": 500}`), causing unhandled promise rejections, `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` fatal crashes, or malformed data frames that corrupt client deserialization.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Applies to any web server layer integrating Web Streams, Node.js streams, Server-Sent Events, or reverse-proxy chunked pipelines.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
export const kHandled = Symbol.for("h3.handled");

export interface StreamPipelineOptions {
  onError: (err: unknown) => void;
}

export async function executeMiddlewareChain(
  event: { headersSent: boolean },
  next: () => Promise<unknown>,
  renderErrorResponse: (err: unknown) => unknown,
): Promise<unknown> {
  try {
    return await next();
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    // Check if the stream or handler has already committed the wire response
    if (error === kHandled || event.headersSent) {
      // Re-throw sentinel to escape middleware chain without rendering secondary error
      throw kHandled;
    }

    // Safe to render clean error response since headers were never committed
    return renderErrorResponse(error);
  }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// ANTI-PATTERN: NEVER blindly catch errors and attempt to write JSON errors on streaming failures
export async function unsafeMiddleware(req: any, res: any, next: any) {
  try {
    await next();
  } catch (err) {
    // FATAL CRASH: If res.write() was called inside next(), this throws ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT
    res.statusCode = 500;
    res.setHeader("content-type", "application/json");
    res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: (err as Error).message }));
  }
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Integration testing with aborted generator streams:
```typescript

it("bypasses error renderer when failure occurs post-stream-commitment", async () => {
  const errorRendererSpy = vi.fn();
  let headersSent = true; // Emulate committed stream state

  const runner = executeMiddlewareChain(
    { headersSent },
    async () => {
      throw kHandled;
    },
    errorRendererSpy
  );

  await expect(runner).rejects.toBe(kHandled);
  expect(errorRendererSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
});
```

**RULE**:
When training Transformer architectures on real-world numerical sequences containing zeros, negative values, and heavy-tailed bursts, systems **MUST** use an invertible, sign-symmetric non-linear scaling transformation such as $\operatorname{arcsinh}(x)$ with local scale normalization, and **MUST NOT** rely on unbounded raw inputs or shifted logarithms ($\ln(x + 1)$).

**WHY**:
Standard shifted log transforms ($\log(x + \epsilon)$) fail when $x < -\epsilon$ (triggering complex numbers or `NaN`), distort negative gradients, and introduce severe bias near zero depending on the choice of arbitrary hyperparameter $\epsilon$. Linear z-score normalization ($ (x - \mu)/\sigma $) collapses when extreme outliers dominate $\sigma$, squashing normal temporal variation into near-zero floating point subnormals ($< 10^{-7}$). $\operatorname{arcsinh}(x)$ behaves linearly for small values ($x \approx 0 \implies \operatorname{arcsinh}(x) \approx x$) and logarithmically for large values ($x \gg 1 \implies \operatorname{arcsinh}(x) \approx \ln(2x)$), natively handling zero and negative values symmetrically without parameter discontinuity.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any continuous sequence representation pipeline (time-series foundation models, telemetry anomaly detectors, tabular tokenizers) where numerical inputs span multiple orders of magnitude with arbitrary signs.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class ArcsinhScaler(nn.Module):
    """
    Symmetric scale-invariant preprocessor with instance-level median absolute deviation (MAD).
    Guarantees strict invertibility and avoids NaN generation across zero/negative values.
    """
    def __init__(self, eps: float = 1e-6):
        super().__init__()
        self.eps = eps

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor = None) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        # x shape: [Batch, Channels, Time]
        if mask is not None:
            valid_x = torch.where(mask.bool(), x, torch.nan)
            loc = torch.nanmedian(valid_x, dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
            loc = torch.nan_to_num(loc, nan=0.0)
            diff = torch.abs(valid_x - loc)
            scale = torch.nanmedian(diff, dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
            scale = torch.nan_to_num(scale, nan=1.0)
        else:
            loc = torch.median(x, dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
            diff = torch.abs(x - loc)
            scale = torch.median(diff, dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
            
        scale = torch.clamp(scale, min=self.eps)
        
        # Standardize then apply arcsinh
        normalized = (x - loc) / scale
        transformed = torch.arcsinh(normalized)
        
        return transformed, loc, scale

    def inverse(self, transformed: torch.Tensor, loc: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Inverse transform: sinh(z) * scale + loc
        sinh_scaled = torch.sinh(transformed)
        return (sinh_scaled * scale) + loc
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:

```python
    # Crashes with NaNs if any x <= -eps
    # Non-symmetric gradient around zero produces asymmetric distributional skew
    return torch.log(x + eps)
```

Assert that `inverse(forward(x))` reconstructs $x$ within relative error tolerance $\epsilon_{\text{rel}} \le 10^{-4}$ and that intermediate tensors contain zero `NaN` or `Inf` flags.

**RULE**:
When mapping high-frequency or long-context continuous time series into patch tokens for transformer architectures, tokenizers **MUST** enforce temporal alignment invariants where context length $T_{\text{context}}$ and horizon $H_{\text{pred}}$ are strictly integer-divisible by `patch_size`, and left-padding **MUST** be used to prevent right-boundary leakage.

**WHY**:
Right-padding causes prediction heads to condition on artificial trailing padding tokens immediately adjacent to the forecast horizon, skewing attention weights at the forecast boundary. If sequences are not integer multiples of `patch_stride`, partial patches drop trailing historical data points (TOCTOU between actual input series end and patch token sequence boundary), corrupting phase and high-frequency cyclical signals at the exact forecast horizon transition.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Patch-based tokenizers, 1D CNN sequence models, and multi-resolution encoders processing variable-length temporal sequences.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class TemporalPatchTokenizer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, patch_size: int = 16, patch_stride: int = 16, d_model: int = 768):
        super().__init__()
        assert patch_size == patch_stride, "Non-overlapping patches required for non-redundant state tokenization."
        self.patch_size = patch_size
        self.patch_stride = patch_stride
        self.proj = nn.Conv1d(
            in_channels=1,
            out_channels=d_model,
            kernel_size=patch_size,
            stride=patch_stride,
            bias=False
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, int]:
        # x: [Batch, Time]
        batch_size, seq_len = x.shape
        remainder = seq_len % self.patch_size
        pad_len = 0
        
        if remainder != 0:
            pad_len = self.patch_size - remainder
            # CRITICAL: Left-pad history so the most recent data point aligns exactly with the last patch
            x = F.pad(x, (pad_len, 0), mode="replicate")
            
        # x: [Batch, 1, Padded_Time]
        x_in = x.unsqueeze(1)
        # patches: [Batch, d_model, Num_Patches] -> [Batch, Num_Patches, d_model]
        tokens = self.proj(x_in).transpose(1, 2)
        return tokens, pad_len
```

**RULE**:
Multi-quantile regression heads emitting simultaneous quantiles $\tau_1 < \tau_2 < \dots < \tau_K$ **MUST** enforce monotonic non-decreasing quantile values either via monotonic activation layers (e.g., cumulative softmax / sort) or evaluate an explicit non-crossing invariant check before downstream consumer emission.

**WHY**:
Independent linear projection heads emitting multiple quantiles inevitably produce quantile crossings ($\hat{q}_{\tau_a} > \hat{q}_{\tau_b}$ for $\tau_a < \tau_b$) under out-of-distribution inputs. When downstream industrial systems use these predictions for safety stock, Value-at-Risk (VaR), or capacity planning, inverted quantiles induce negative probability distributions, catastrophic under-hedging, and immediate runtime assertions in downstream pricing engines.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All direct non-autoregressive multi-quantile forecasting networks emitting tabular, temporal, or spatial distributions.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class MonotonicQuantileHead(nn.Module):
    """
    Guarantees strict quantile monotonicity: Q(tau_1) <= Q(tau_2) <= ... <= Q(tau_K)
    using base prediction plus cumulative softplus offsets.
    """
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, num_patches: int, patch_size: int, num_quantiles: int = 21):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_patches = num_patches
        self.patch_size = patch_size
        self.num_quantiles = num_quantiles
        
        # Base projection for median / first quantile
        self.base_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, num_patches * patch_size)
        # Offset projections for subsequent quantiles
        self.offset_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, num_patches * patch_size * (num_quantiles - 1))

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x: [Batch, Context_Tokens, d_model] -> pool or select regression token
        reg_token = x[:, -1, :] # [Batch, d_model]
        batch_size = reg_token.shape[0]
        
        q0 = self.base_proj(reg_token).view(batch_size, self.num_patches * self.patch_size, 1)
        offsets = self.offset_proj(reg_token).view(batch_size, self.num_patches * self.patch_size, self.num_quantiles - 1)
        
        # Softplus ensures all subsequent quantile steps are strictly positive
        positive_offsets = nn.functional.softplus(offsets)
        
        # Cumulative sum enforces q_{k} = q_0 + sum_{i=1}^k delta_i
        quantiles = torch.cat([q0, q0 + torch.cumsum(positive_offsets, dim=-1)], dim=-1)
        # Output shape: [Batch, Horizon, Num_Quantiles]
        return quantiles
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:

```python
        super().__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(d_model, horizon * num_quantiles)

        # Unconstrained outputs will cross in OOD regimes (e.g. q_0.95 < q_0.50)
        return self.linear(x).view(x.shape[0], -1, 21)
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image) (Revision: `hf-comfy-o`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When serving large-scale multi-modal diffusion architectures, execution engines **MUST NOT** bind the text encoder, diffusion backbone, and variational autoencoder (VAE) to a monolithic precision target. Systems **MUST** partition weights into isolated single-purpose checkpoints allowing independent quantization profiles (`bf16`, `int8`, `w4a8`) per subsystem.

**WHY**:
Binding disparate multi-modal components into a single checkpoint forces identical quantization on all sub-networks. Text encoders (such as `Qwen3.5-9B`) are memory-bound and sensitive to activation outliers, benefiting from activation-rotation (`convrot`) or `W4A8` GPTQ, whereas diffusion backbones require high dimensional dynamic ranges (`bf16` or `fp8_e4m3fn`) to avoid visual artifacts (e.g., color banding, dynamic range compression). Monolithic packaging causes catastrophic out-of-memory (OOM) errors on consumer hardware or degrades generative fidelity by over-quantizing the denoiser.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to any multi-modal diffusion or autoregressive pipeline where the total combined parameter count exceeds the high-water mark of consumer accelerator memory (e.g., 16GB–24GB VRAM) and distinct components exhibit varying sensitivity to numerical precision degradation.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
# Safe, decoupled multi-state loader invariant
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import safetensors.torch
import torch

class DecoupledModelLoader:
    """Enforces isolated precision loads across model boundaries."""
    
    SUPPORTED_BACKBONE_DTYPES = {
        "bf16": torch.bfloat16,
        "fp8_e4m3fn": torch.float8_e4m3fn,
        "int8": torch.int8
    }
    
    SUPPORTED_TEXT_DTYPES = {
        "bf16": torch.bfloat16,
        "w4a8_gptq": torch.int32,  # Packed integer containers
        "int8_convrot": torch.int8
    }

    def __init__(self, root_models_dir: Path):
        self.root = root_models_dir
        self.diffusion_dir = root_models_dir / "diffusion_models"
        self.text_dir = root_models_dir / "text_encoders"
        self.vae_dir = root_models_dir / "vae"

    def load_subsystem_tensor_slice(
        self, 
        subsystem: str, 
        filename: str, 
        device: torch.device
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        target_path = (self.root / subsystem / filename).resolve()
        
        # Enforce directory containment boundary to prevent path traversal
        if not target_path.is_file() or not target_path.as_posix().startswith(self.root.resolve().as_posix()):
            raise ValueError(f"Security invariant violation: Invalid path resolution for {target_path}")

        # Open safetensors handle without pulling entire buffer into RAM simultaneously
        loaded_tensors: Dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
        with safetensors.safe_open(target_path, framework="pt", device=str(device)) as f:
            for k in f.keys():
                loaded_tensors[k] = f.get_tensor(k)
        return loaded_tensors
```

**RULE**:
Any model repository downstream repack **MUST** provide an explicit deterministic directory schema and safetensors metadata layout where layer prefixes strictly conform to subsystem namespaces (`diffusion_models/`, `text_encoders/`, `vae/`) and **MUST NOT** rely on implicit key guessing or regex heuristics at runtime.

**WHY**:
ComfyUI's model routing uses directory placement to instantiate model architectures. When models are distributed without deterministic naming and decoupled directory topologies, the runtime loader falls back to inspecting all tensor keys across tens of gigabytes of data. This induces disk I/O thrashing, stalls user thread execution, and results in catastrophic silent fallback to incorrect model classes (e.g., attempting to load a `Qwen3.5` text encoder as an SDXL CLIP model).

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
When repackaging, distributing, or orchestrating local deployment of heterogeneous diffusion models containing multiple modular sub-networks.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Set

EXPECTED_TOPOLOGY = {
    "diffusion_models": {"moss_image_base_bf16.safetensors", "moss_image_sft_bf16.safetensors"},
    "text_encoders": {"qwen3.5_9b_bf16.safetensors", "qwen3.5_9b_int8_convrot.safetensors"},
    "vae": {"flux2-vae.safetensors", "flux2-vae_small.safetensors"}
}

def verify_comfy_directory_layout(root_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Verifies that ComfyUI directory structure matches strict invariants."""
    for subfolder, valid_files in EXPECTED_TOPOLOGY.items():
        folder_path = root_dir / subfolder
        if not folder_path.exists() or not folder_path.is_dir():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing mandatory architectural subfolder: {subfolder}")
        
        discovered_files = {p.name for p in folder_path.glob("*.safetensors")}
        # Invariant: At least one recognized candidate must be present per partition
        if not discovered_files.intersection(valid_files) and len(discovered_files) == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Partition '{subfolder}' does not contain recognized model weights.")
```

PROVENANCE_END -->
> **Provenance**: Harvested from [facebook/docusaurus](https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus) (Revision: `7b6826b8`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When sharing mutable state, singletons, or in-memory caches between compilers or pipeline stages via loader/plugin options objects, you **MUST NOT** pass the raw collection object (such as `Map`, `Set`, or class instance). You **MUST** pass a zero-argument accessor closure (getter function, e.g., `() => cacheInstance`).

**WHY**:
Third-party build instrumentation tools, diagnostic plugins (e.g., Rsdoctor, Webpack Bundle Analyzer), or worker serialization boundaries perform deep structural cloning (`structuredClone`, `lodash.cloneDeep`, or JSON-roundtrips) on configuration and loader option trees. 
1. Deep-cloning a `Map` or `Set` across loader stages disconnects the shared reference, breaking cache coherence and causing client/server dual compilations to execute redundant, heavy work.
2. If the deep-clone implementation only clones enumerable plain properties, a `Map` instance is converted into an empty plain object `{}`. Any subsequent invocation of `crossCompilerCache.get()` or `.has()` immediately crashes with a runtime `TypeError: cache.get is not a function`.
Because functions are non-enumerable primitives that cannot be structurally cloned as data, cloning engines retain function references as-is.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any build plugin, Webpack loader, Vite plugin, or micro-frontend configuration where options are shared across multiple compiler instances (e.g., client bundle + SSR bundle) or passed through intermediate bundler transforms.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
// packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/options.ts & loader.ts

export type CrossCompilerCache = Map<string, PromiseWithResolvers<string>>;

export type LoaderOptions = {
  /**
   * Getter returning the shared cache instance.
   * Passing a getter protects the cache reference from being stripped
   * or corrupted into a plain object by deep-cloning tools (e.g., Rsdoctor).
   */
  getCrossCompilerCache?: () => CrossCompilerCache;
};

// Instantiation: Scope the cache instance inside the orchestrator closure
export function createLoaderConfig(): { loader: string; options: LoaderOptions } {
  const sharedCache: CrossCompilerCache = new Map();

  return {
    loader: require.resolve('./loader'),
    options: {
      getCrossCompilerCache: () => sharedCache,
    },
  };
}

// Consumer: Dereference via the getter inside the loader execution context
export async function executeLoader(options: LoaderOptions, cacheKey: string): Promise<string> {
  const cache = options.getCrossCompilerCache?.();
  
  if (!cache) {
    return runDirectCompilation();
  }

  const existingEntry = cache.get(cacheKey);
  if (existingEntry) {
    return existingEntry.promise;
  }

  const resolvers = Promise.withResolvers<string>();
  cache.set(cacheKey, resolvers);

  try {
    const result = await runDirectCompilation();
    resolvers.resolve(result);
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    resolvers.reject(error);
    cache.delete(cacheKey); // Evict on failure to allow retry
    throw error;
  }
}
```

**RULE**:
When configuring persistent compiler or build caches (e.g., Webpack Persistent Cache, Rspack cache, Turbo remote cache), the cache version identifier **MUST** be composed as a composite deterministic hash incorporating the exact values of all **downstream build environment dependencies**, including target environment queries (`Browserslist`), module aliases, and asset parser size limits—not merely compiler version and source hashes.

**WHY**:
Bundler loaders (such as Babel, SWC, or PostCSS) and minimizers (such as Terser, Esbuild, or CSSNano) derive their transpilation targets, syntax downgrades, polyfills, and CSS transformations dynamically from external configuration files (e.g., `.browserslistrc`, `package.json -> browserslist`, or environment flags). 
Webpack and Rspack persistent caches track source file contents and compiler package versions, but do **NOT** track runtime options loaded dynamically inside external loader/minimizer sub-dependencies. Modifying the target browser profile (e.g., from modern browsers to legacy Safari/Chrome) without touching code files will serve stale, un-polyfilled cache hits, causing production whiteouts and unhandled syntax errors.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any static site generator, bundler harness, or CLI build tool employing filesystem/disk persistent caching mechanisms (`cache.type = 'filesystem'`).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
// packages/docusaurus/src/webpack/base.ts
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { getBrowserslistQueries } from '@docusaurus/bundler';

function md5Hash(content: string): string {
  return crypto.createHash('md5').update(content).digest('hex');
}

export function computeCacheVersion({
  docusaurusVersion,
  themeAliases,
  assetInlineMaxSize,
}: {
  docusaurusVersion: string;
  themeAliases: Record<string, string>;
  assetInlineMaxSize: number;
}): string {
  // 1. Alias change hash: Webpack does not automatically bust cache on alias overrides
  const themeAliasesHash = md5Hash(JSON.stringify(themeAliases));
  
  // 2. Browserslist change hash: Loader/minimizer downleveling changes with target queries
  const browserslistQueries = getBrowserslistQueries();
  const browserslistHash = md5Hash(JSON.stringify(browserslistQueries));

  // 3. Asset configuration changes: Dictates inline base64 vs external file emission
  return `${docusaurusVersion}-${themeAliasesHash}-${browserslistHash}-${assetInlineMaxSize}`;
}
```

**RULE**:
When an application uses an isolated internal instance of a library that relies on global runtime bindings (e.g., `Prism`, `window.Prism`, or custom polyfills), dynamic extensions or language definitions **MUST NOT** unconditionally delete the global reference upon registration completion if downstream hooks or evaluation routines depend on accessing the global instance during rendering. If a prior foreign instance existed before registration, it **MUST** be restored; otherwise, the isolated instance **MUST** remain anchored.

**WHY**:
Legacy libraries and syntax highlighters (e.g., Prism component plugins such as `twig`, `liquid`, `markup-templating`) register language hooks that execute lazily on every highlight invocation. These hooks reference `globalThis.Prism` directly at execution time rather than referencing the local closure instance passed to the loader. 
Executing `delete globalThis.Prism` immediately after module loading prevents initialization crashes, but detonates every subsequent code-block render with `ReferenceError: Prism is not defined`. Furthermore, naively restoring previous instances without checking if a preexisting global was present can clobber foreign third-party highlighters (such as embedded Swagger/Redoc instances).

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
When wrapping non-ESM legacy libraries, syntax highlighters, markdown parsers, or global runtime polyfills inside modern modular frameworks (React/Vite/Webpack).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
// packages/docusaurus-theme-classic/src/theme/prism-include-languages.ts
import type * as PrismNamespace from 'prismjs';

const MarkupTemplatingLanguages = [
  'django', 'ejs', 'erb', 'etlua', 'ftl', 'handlebars',
  'latte', 'liquid', 'php', 'smarty', 'soy', 'tt2', 'twig'
] as const;

export default function prismIncludeLanguages(
  PrismObject: typeof PrismNamespace,
  additionalLanguages: string[]
): void {
  // Capture prior global state (e.g., Redoc, Swagger, or legacy script tags)
  const PrismBefore = (globalThis as { Prism?: typeof PrismNamespace }).Prism;

  // Mount internal instance onto global scope for language registrations
  (globalThis as { Prism?: typeof PrismNamespace }).Prism = PrismObject;

  try {
    for (const lang of additionalLanguages) {
      if (MarkupTemplatingLanguages.includes(lang as any)) {
        // Enforce prerequisite registration before dependent grammars load
        require('prismjs/components/prism-markup-templating.js');
      }
      require(`prismjs/components/prism-${lang}`);
    }
  } finally {
    // If a foreign instance pre-existed, restore it to avoid clobbering host.
    // If NO instance existed prior, LEAVE OUR INSTANCE MOUNTED because
    // grammars like 'twig' and 'liquid' execute hooks reading `globalThis.Prism`
    // at highlight time!
    if (typeof PrismBefore !== 'undefined') {
      (globalThis as { Prism?: typeof PrismNamespace }).Prism = PrismBefore;
    }
  }
}
```

**RULE**:
When initializing an in-memory SQLite database connection pool (`sqlite::memory:`) in an asynchronous multi-threaded runtime (e.g., Tokio), the connection pool MUST configured with a connection ceiling (`max_connections > 1`), a warm baseline (`min_connections >= 2`), a deterministic acquisition timeout (`acquire_timeout`), and finite connection lifespans (`idle_timeout`, `max_lifetime`). You MUST NOT configure `max_connections(1)` under concurrent test runners or parallel task executors.

**WHY**:
In asynchronous execution models where parallel tests or background workers query the database simultaneously, an in-memory connection pool capped at 1 causes complete thread starvation and deadlocks on nested or concurrent queries (e.g., an asynchronous task holding a connection during a transaction while awaiting a sub-query that requests a second connection from the same pool). Furthermore, without explicit `acquire_timeout` settings, stalled tasks block indefinitely, exhausting Tokio worker queues without emitting actionable diagnostic traces.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to any Rust (`sqlx`, `diesel`), Go (`database/sql`), or Node.js (`better-sqlite3`) service utilizing in-memory SQLite instances across concurrent test suites, integration fixtures, or ephemeral embedded databases.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```rust
// ee/tabby-db/src/lib.rs
use std::{str::FromStr, time::Duration};
use sqlx::{sqlite::{SqliteConnectOptions, SqlitePoolOptions}, Pool, Sqlite, Result};

pub struct DbConn {
    pool: Pool<Sqlite>,
}

impl DbConn {
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "testutils"))]
    pub async fn new_in_memory() -> Result<Self> {
        let options = SqliteConnectOptions::from_str("sqlite::memory:")?;
        
        // Explicitly size and guard pool to support concurrent test execution
        let pool: Pool<Sqlite> = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
            .max_connections(20)
            .min_connections(2)
            .acquire_timeout(Duration::from_secs(6))
            .idle_timeout(Duration::from_secs(300))
            .max_lifetime(Duration::from_secs(3600))
            .connect_with(options)
            .await?;

        DbConn::init_db(pool).await
    }

    async fn init_db(pool: Pool<Sqlite>) -> Result<Self> {
        sqlx::migrate!("./migrations").run(&pool).await?;
        Ok(Self { pool })
    }
}
```
