> **Provenance**: Harvested from [o2sh/onefetch](https://github.com/o2sh/onefetch) (Revision: `b5f80988`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When computing metrics between revisions across branches (such as unreleased commits between a release tag and `HEAD`), implementations **MUST NOT** reject the calculation simply because `HEAD` is not a strict descendant of the target tag (i.e., `merge_base(HEAD, tag) != tag`). Instead, implementations **MUST** compute the metric using topological symmetric difference or disjoint revision walk (`tag..HEAD`), which remains algebraically valid on divergent branch topologies and cherry-picked histories.

**WHY**:
In trunk-based development, hotfix branches, and release maintenance branches, `HEAD` frequently diverges from the latest global tag. Asserting that `merge_base == tag` produces false negatives: the system reports zero unreleased changes or omits the status metric completely whenever a fast-forward line is broken by a rebase, merge commit, or out-of-order patch release.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Git metrics collectors, CI/CD changelog generators, release automation engines, and developer dashboard CLIs querying commit intervals between tags/references and current working states.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```rust
use gix::Repository;
use gix::ObjectId;
use anyhow::Result;

pub struct UnreleasedDiff {
    pub tag_name: String,
    pub commits_since_tag: usize,
}

impl UnreleasedDiff {
    /// Computes commits reachable from HEAD but not reachable from latest_tag (tag..HEAD)
    /// without requiring latest_tag to be an ancestor of HEAD.
    pub fn calculate(
        repo: &Repository,
        latest_tag_name: String,
        latest_tag_commit: ObjectId,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let head_id = repo.head_id()?.detach();

        // Safe topological count: tag..HEAD
        // repo.rev_walk([head_id]) with excluded commit latest_tag_commit
        let commits_since_tag = repo
            .rev_walk([head_id])
            .with_boundary([latest_tag_commit])
            .all()?
            .try_fold(0usize, |count, info| -> Result<usize> {
                let _commit_info = info?;
                Ok(count.saturating_add(1))
            })?;

        Ok(Self {
            tag_name: latest_tag_name,
            commits_since_tag,
        })
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```rust
// ANTI-PATTERN: Demanding strict lineage causes false negatives on non-fast-forward branches
pub fn calculate_bad(repo: &Repository, tag_id: ObjectId) -> Result<Option<usize>> {
    let head_id = repo.head_id()?.detach();
    let merge_base = repo.merge_base(head_id, tag_id)?;
    
    // BREAKS: If HEAD is on a maintenance branch or rebased past the tag,
    // merge_base is an ancestor of the tag, NOT the tag itself.
    if merge_base.map(|id| id.detach()) != Some(tag_id) {
        return Ok(None); // Silently swallows metric!
    }

    // rev-list tag..HEAD
    Ok(Some(count_commits(repo, tag_id, head_id)?))
}
```

2. Commit `C2` on `branch-A`.
3. Branch from `C1` to `branch-B`, commit `C3`.
4. Run the calculation on `branch-B` with `tag = v1.0.0`.
Assert that `commits_since_tag == 1` and does not return `None` or an ancestral verification error.

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [o2sh/onefetch](https://github.com/o2sh/onefetch) (Revision: `b5f80988`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When parsing, measuring, or slicing formatted text containing terminal color tokens or escape sequences (e.g., `{0}`, ANSI CSI codes `\x1b[...m`), the visual layout engine **MUST** decouple raw byte length and character count from printable terminal cell width. Slicing operations and bounding box calculations **MUST** decrement cursor widths strictly on visual/printable tokens, while permitting non-printable/style tokens to bypass bounding bounds without advancing character coordinates.

**WHY**:
Treating color/style tags as printable characters causes column misalignment, jagged ASCII rendering, and broken formatting strings. Conversely, stripping tags prior to truncation destroys color boundaries, leading to ANSI color bleed across terminal rows.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any terminal renderer, CLI syntax highlighter, text-wrapping algorithm, or column-based layout formatter handling ANSI escapes or custom templating markup.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum LayoutToken {
    StyleDirective(u32),
    PrintableChar(char),
    Whitespace,
}

impl LayoutToken {
    #[inline]
    pub fn visual_width(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            LayoutToken::PrintableChar(_) | LayoutToken::Whitespace => 1,
            LayoutToken::StyleDirective(_) => 0,
        }
    }
}

pub struct TokenStream<'a>(&'a str);

impl<'a> TokenStream<'a> {
    pub fn truncate_visible(
        tokens: impl Iterator<Item = LayoutToken>,
        mut start_col: usize,
        end_col: usize,
    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = LayoutToken> {
        let mut visual_width = end_col.saturating_sub(start_col);

        tokens
            // Phase 1: Skip leading visible characters up to start_col without skipping styling
            .filter(move |tok| {
                let w = tok.visual_width();
                if start_col > 0 && w > 0 {
                    start_col = start_col.saturating_sub(w);
                    return false;
                }
                true
            })
            // Phase 2: Take tokens until printable width is exhausted, keeping inline trailing styles safe
            .take_while(move |tok| {
                let w = tok.visual_width();
                if visual_width == 0 && w > 0 {
                    return false;
                }
                visual_width = visual_width.saturating_sub(w);
                true
            })
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```rust
// ANTI-PATTERN: Operating directly on raw strings or characters without width differentiation
pub fn bad_truncate(input: &str, start: usize, len: usize) -> String {
    // Slicing on char indices cuts across {n} tokens mid-sequence,
    // corrupts terminal escape codes, and miscalculates visual columns.
    input.chars().skip(start).take(len).collect()
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Property test with arbitrary ASCII strings interspersed with `{0}`..`{9}` and `\x1b[38;5;Xm` tags. Assert that the visual width of the emitted line (`stripped of styling`) exactly equals `min(end_col - start_col, original_visual_width)`.

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [LiconStudio/Minimax-H3-VBVR](https://huggingface.co/LiconStudio/Minimax-H3-VBVR) (Revision: `hf-liconst`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When extending a large, frozen foundation model (LLM, Diffusion, Vision) with specific domain behaviors (e.g., physics, style, language), you MUST use Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) or similar parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods rather than full fine-tuning, UNLESS the domain shift is so fundamental that the base architecture is incompatible.
**WHY**:
Full fine-tuning destroys the generalization capabilities of the base model (catastrophic forgetting) and requires massive VRAM (often >80GB for 7B+ models). LoRA decomposes the weight update $\Delta W$ into two smaller matrices $A$ and $B$ ($\Delta W = BA$), reducing trainable parameters by 100x-1000x. This allows multiple specialized adapters to be loaded/unloaded dynamically, preserving the base model's integrity and enabling "hot-swapping" of capabilities.
**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any scenario where a pre-trained model needs to be specialized for a niche task (e.g., medical imaging, legal text, specific video physics) without retraining the entire backbone.
**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
# Pseudocode for LoRA Integration in a Diffusion Model
import torch
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

# 1. Load Base Model (Frozen)
base_model = load_diffusion_model("MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3")
for param in base_model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False

# 2. Define LoRA Config
lora_config = LoraConfig(
    r=16,  # Rank of the low-rank matrices
    lora_alpha=32,
    target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"], # Attention layers
    lora_dropout=0.05
)

# 3. Wrap Model with LoRA
model_with_lora = get_peft_model(base_model, lora_config)

# 4. Train ONLY the LoRA parameters
# The base model weights remain frozen in memory
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model_with_lora.parameters(), lr=1e-4)
```
**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```python
# ANTI-PATTERN: Full Fine-Tuning for a Niche Task
# This wastes VRAM, risks catastrophic forgetting, and makes the model
# unusable for other tasks without retraining.
for param in base_model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = True # DANGEROUS: Unfreezes entire backbone
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(base_model.parameters(), lr=1e-5)
```
**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
1.  **Parameter Count Check:** Assert that `trainable_params / total_params < 0.01` (1%).
2.  **Memory Profiling:** Verify that VRAM usage during training is significantly lower than full fine-tuning (e.g., <20GB for a 7B model vs >80GB).
3.  **Generalization Test:** Evaluate the base model (without LoRA) on a general task to ensure it remains intact if the LoRA is removed.

**RULE**:
When training or validating video generation models, you MUST implement automated or semi-automated comparative validation that explicitly measures **object persistence** and **spatial collision** metrics, rather than relying solely on aesthetic quality scores (e.g., FID, CLIP Score).
**WHY**:
Standard metrics (FID, CLIP) measure distribution similarity and semantic alignment but are blind to physical plausibility. A video can have high FID (looks realistic) but contain objects passing through walls (low physical consistency). Explicitly tracking object identity across frames and checking for interpenetration is required to verify "physics" improvements.
**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any video generation model training or evaluation where physical realism, object permanence, or character interaction is a key requirement.
**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
# Pseudocode for Physics-Aware Video Validation
def validate_video_physics(video_frames, object_tracker):
    """
    video_frames: List of numpy arrays (H, W, C)
    object_tracker: Model to track object IDs across frames
    """
    object_ids = object_tracker.track(video_frames)
    
    # 1. Check Object Persistence (No Duplication)
    # If an object ID appears in two disjoint spatial regions in the same frame, it's a duplication error.
    for frame_idx, frame in enumerate(video_frames):
        detections = object_tracker.get_detections(frame_idx)
        unique_ids = set(det['id'] for det in detections)
        if len(detections) != len(unique_ids):
            return {"pass": False, "error": "Object Duplication Detected"}
            
    # 2. Check Interpenetration (Simplified Bounding Box Overlap)
    # If two distinct object bounding boxes overlap significantly, it's a collision error.
    for frame_idx in range(len(video_frames) - 1):
        dets_curr = object_tracker.get_detections(frame_idx)
        dets_next = object_tracker.get_detections(frame_idx + 1)
        # Check IoU (Intersection over Union) for distinct IDs
        for d1 in dets_curr:
            for d2 in dets_next:
                if d1['id'] != d2['id']:
                    iou = calculate_iou(d1['bbox'], d2['bbox'])
                    if iou > 0.5: # Threshold for significant overlap
                        return {"pass": False, "error": "Interpenetration Detected"}
                        
    return {"pass": True}
```

```python
# because the frames look individually realistic.

    print("Model is good") # FALSE POSITIVE for physics errors
```

**RULE**:
When serializing composite nested structures into byte buffers (`bytes.Buffer`) or string builders (`strings.Builder`), the caller MUST pre-calculate the exact total byte allocation via a dedicated pass (`formatLen()`) and invoke `Grow(n)` exactly once at the top level. The program MUST NOT invoke `.Grow()` inside individual child element emitters.

**WHY**:
Invoking `.Grow(len)` incrementally inside inner loops causes amortized geometric slice reallocations (`runtime.growslice`). Each intermediate resize copies old memory buffers, creates heap fragmentation, triggers GC write barriers, and saturates CPU cache lines. Pre-computing lengths uses $O(N)$ integer arithmetic (CPU register operations) to prevent $O(N \log N)$ reallocation and memory copy overhead.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to any high-throughput serialization routine, KV-store key generation, network packet marshalling, or logging pipeline in Go, Rust, or C++.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```go
// pkg/labels/array.go & pkg/labels/labels.go pattern
func (l *Label) formatLen() int {
	n := len(l.Source) + len(SourceDelimiter) + len(l.Key)
	if len(l.Value) != 0 {
		n += 1 + len(l.Value) // Accounts for '=' delimiter
	}
	return n
}

func (ls LabelArray) formatLen() int {
	// 2 bytes for '[' and ']', plus 1 byte separator per element after index 0
	n := 2 + max(len(ls)-1, 0)
	for l := range ls {
		n += ls[l].formatLen()
	}
	return n
}

func (ls LabelArray) BuildString(sb *strings.Builder) {
	// Single top-level allocation reserving the exact heap footprint
	sb.Grow(ls.formatLen())
	sb.WriteByte('[')
	for l := range ls {
		if l > 0 {
			sb.WriteByte(';')
		}
		// Inner serializer writes directly without calling sb.Grow()
		ls[l].buildStringNoGrow(sb)
	}
	sb.WriteByte(']')
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```go
// ANTI-PATTERN: Inner method growing the builder iteratively inside loops
func (l *Label) BuildString(sb *strings.Builder) {
	// ANTI-PATTERN: Calling Grow on every nested token forces repeated 
	// re-allocation when builder capacity is exceeded.
	sb.Grow(len(l.Source) + len(SourceDelimiter) + len(l.Key) + len(l.Value) + 1)
	sb.WriteString(l.Source)
	sb.WriteString(SourceDelimiter)
	sb.WriteString(l.Key)
	if len(l.Value) != 0 {
		sb.WriteByte('=')
		sb.WriteString(l.Value)
	}
}

func (ls LabelArray) BuildStringBad(sb *strings.Builder) {
	sb.WriteByte('[')
	for l := range ls {
		ls[l].BuildString(sb) // Triggers reallocation churn on large label arrays
	}
	sb.WriteByte(']')
}
```

```go
	labels := GenerateTestLabels(100)
	b.ReportAllocs()
	b.ResetTimer()
	for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
		var sb strings.Builder
		labels.BuildString(&sb)
	}
	// Assert that allocs/op == 1 (the underlying String() string buffer allocation)
	if allocs := testing.AllocsPerRun(1000, func() {
		var sb strings.Builder
		labels.BuildString(&sb)
		_ = sb.String()
	}); allocs > 2.0 {
		b.Fatalf("Expected <= 2 allocations, got %f", allocs)
```

**RULE**:
Internal data structures, API representations, and agent pipelines MUST use immutable, comparable value-typed IP primitives (`net/netip.Addr`, `net/netip.Prefix`) instead of string representations (`string`) or pointer-backed heap structures (`net.IP`, `*net.IPNet`). IP parsing and validation MUST occur strictly at external API deserialization ingress boundaries.

**WHY**:
Strings require heap allocations, dynamic slice headers, and expensive hex/decimal parsing on every lookup. `net.IP` is a `[]byte` slice alias, which means it cannot be compared with `==`, can be mutated concurrently, and causes heap allocations during map indexing. `netip.Addr` is a 24-byte zero-allocation value struct that supports direct equality (`==`), bitwise masking, map keying without hashing allocations, and zero-allocation serialization.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All networking pipelines, control planes, cgroup management structures, and container metadata caches handling IP addresses and CIDR subnets.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```go
// pkg/cgroups/manager/manager.go pattern
package manager

import (
	"log/slog"
	"net/netip"
	v1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
)

type PodMetadata struct {
	Name      string
	Namespace string
	IPs       []netip.Addr // Value types, zero heap overhead per address
}

func (m *cgroupManager) updatePodMetadata(pod *v1.Pod) {
	podIPs := pod.Status.PodIPs
	ips := make([]netip.Addr, 0, len(podIPs))
	
	for _, podIP := range podIPs {
		ip, err := netip.ParseAddr(podIP.IP)
		if err != nil {
			m.logger.Debug("failed to parse pod IP",
				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
				slog.String("pod", pod.Name),
				slog.String("rawIP", podIP.IP),
			)
			continue
		}
		ips = append(ips, ip)
	}
	m.storeIPs(pod.UID, ips)
}
```

**RULE**:
Per-CPU contextual scratchpad memory that persists across eBPF tail calls within single-packet processing MUST be implemented using static ELF auxiliary variables (`auxvar` mapped into per-CPU data sections) rather than `BPF_MAP_TYPE_PERCPU_ARRAY` maps.

**WHY**:
Invoking `bpf_map_lookup_elem()` on a `BPF_MAP_TYPE_PERCPU_ARRAY` introduces register spills, pointer validation branches, and verifier complexity for array bounds and null pointer verification. Auxvars resolve to direct memory dereferences off the per-CPU base pointer (`AUX_REUSE`) with zero function call overhead and compile-time bounds checks via `build_bug_on()`.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
XDP and TC programs where metadata must survive packet truncation or `bpf_tail_call()` executions, emulating `__sk_buff->cb[]`.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```c
// bpf/include/bpf/ctx/xdp.h & bpf/lib/auxvars.h pattern
struct cilium_xdp_scratch {
	__u32 data[META_PIVOT / sizeof(__u32)];
};

DEFINE_AUX(struct cilium_xdp_scratch, cilium_xdp_scratch);

static __always_inline void ctx_store_meta(struct xdp_md *ctx, const __u64 off, __u32 datum)
{
	struct cilium_xdp_scratch *scratch = AUX_REUSE(cilium_xdp_scratch);

	scratch->data[off] = datum;
	// Compile-time boundary verification enforced via LLVM built-in
	build_bug_on((off + 1) * sizeof(__u32) > META_PIVOT);
}

static __always_inline __u32 ctx_load_meta(const struct xdp_md *ctx, const __u64 off)
{
	struct cilium_xdp_scratch *scratch = AUX_REUSE(cilium_xdp_scratch);

	build_bug_on((off + 1) * sizeof(__u32) > META_PIVOT);
	return scratch->data[off];
}
```

```c
	__uint(max_entries, 1);

{
```

- If `DB_PASSWORD` is updated in `.env` but `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is missed in `.env.rag`, the platform starts while background graph ingestion fails silently.

```python
from __future__ import annotations

PLATFORM_SECRETS_WHITELIST: Set[str] = {
    "JWT_SECRET", "GATEWAY_API_KEY", "INTERNAL_API_KEY",
    "MCP_KEY_SECRET", "DATA_SOURCE_SECRET_KEY", "DB_PASSWORD"
}

# Invariant 2: Explicit equality groups spanning divergent variable names
CROSS_KEY_EQUALITY_GROUPS: List[List[str]] = [
    ["DB_PASSWORD", "POSTGRES_PASSWORD"],
    ["MINIO_ROOT_USER", "MINIO_ACCESS_KEY"],
    ["MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD", "MINIO_SECRET_KEY"],
]

def audit_secret_consistency(env_files: Dict[Path, Dict[str, str]]) -> List[str]:
    violations: List[str] = []
    
    # Check 1: Cross-file same-name invariant
    all_keys = {k for d in env_files.values() for k in d.keys()}
    for k in all_keys:
        if k in PLATFORM_SECRETS_WHITELIST:
            seen_values: Dict[str, Path] = {}
            for path, env_dict in env_files.items():
                val = env_dict.get(k)
                if val:
                    if not seen_values:
                        seen_values[val] = path
                    elif val not in seen_values:
                        primary_val, primary_path = next(iter(seen_values.items()))
                        violations.append(
                            f"DRIFT: {k} in {path.name} differs from {primary_path.name}"
                        )
                        
    # Check 2: Cross-key group invariant
    for group in CROSS_KEY_EQUALITY_GROUPS:
        resolved_vals: Dict[str, tuple[str, Path]] = {}
        for path, env_dict in env_files.items():
            for key in group:
                if key in env_dict and env_dict[key]:
                    resolved_vals[key] = (env_dict[key], path)
        if len(set(v[0] for v in resolved_vals.values())) > 1:
            violations.append(f"GROUP DRIFT: Values for {group} do not match across stack: {resolved_vals}")

    return violations
```

**RULE**:
In knowledge compilation and RAG pipelines, an extracted factual claim **MUST NOT** achieve status `SUPPORTED` unless it is bound to one or more verified, immutable `SourceSpan` records. Each `SourceSpan` **MUST** cryptographically bind the source hash, chunk identifier, start character offset, end character offset, and exact character payload. Factual claims with unresolvable or missing evidence **MUST** fail closed to `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` or `REFUTED`.

**WHY**:
Allowing LLM synthesizers to output claims with loose, page-level, or unverified document-level references causes hallucination leaks. Without character-offset and document-hash locking, downstream document mutations or parser alterations render previously asserted claims untraceable. If the underlying document changes, claims referencing old offsets must be discarded or marked unverified rather than re-bound on title alone.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All systems processing enterprise documents, legal knowledge bases, compliance corpora, and factual QA engines where hallucination carries legal or operational liability.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
# jonex_wiki/domain/engine/compile/content_validation.py
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator, ConfigDict
from typing import List, Literal

class SourceSpan(BaseModel):
    passage_id: str
    source_id: str
    document_id: str
    chunk_id: str
    passage_text_sha256: str
    start_char: int
    end_char: int
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

class ValidatedClaim(BaseModel):
    claim_id: str
    page_path: str
    text: str
    evidence: List[EvidenceRef] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)
    unresolved_evidence: List[EvidenceRef] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)
    source_spans: List[SourceSpan] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)
    support_status: Literal["SUPPORTED", "REFUTED", "NOT_ENOUGH_INFO"] = "NOT_ENOUGH_INFO"
    support_reason: str = "support_not_evaluated"

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def enforce_grounded_evidence_binding(self):
        # Invariant 1: SUPPORTED claims MUST have physical source spans
        if self.support_status in ("SUPPORTED", "REFUTED") and not self.source_spans:
            raise ValueError(f"Status '{self.support_status}' requires at least one valid SourceSpan")
        
        # Invariant 2: Cannot claim SUPPORTED if any evidence failed resolution
        if self.support_status == "SUPPORTED" and self.unresolved_evidence:
            raise ValueError("SUPPORTED claims cannot contain unresolved evidence references")
            
        # Invariant 3: Spans must bind to resolved evidence
        evidence_identities = {
            (r.passage_id, r.source_id, r.document_id, r.chunk_id) 
            for r in self.evidence
        }
        for span in self.source_spans:
            span_id = (span.passage_id, span.source_id, span.document_id, span.chunk_id)
            if span_id not in evidence_identities:
                raise ValueError("SourceSpan references evidence not present in resolved evidence list")
        return self
```

**RULE**:
All production security guards asserting key entropy, token complexity, or default sentinel detection **MUST NOT** branch conditionally on environment variables like `ENV == "prod"` when evaluating system-critical secrets. They **MUST** evaluate unconditionally, utilizing explicit opt-in override flags (`ALLOW_INSECURE_JWT_SECRET=true`) only for local development.

**WHY**:
Relying on `config.is_production` or `ENV == "prod"` introduces a catastrophic failure mode: when a production container is deployed without an explicit `ENV=prod` variable, it defaults silently to `ENV="dev"`. Under conditional guards, this causes production instances to run with well-known sentinel strings (`change-me-in-production`, `your_jwt_secret_key_here_...`), leaving them vulnerable to unauthenticated admin JWT forging, arbitrary tenant data injection, and signature spoofing.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Startup lifecycle of all backend systems, API Gateways, and microservices managing JWT validation, cryptographic signature verification, or database encryption.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
# jonex_core/common/security_guards.py
import os
from typing import Set

_INSECURE_SENTINELS: Set[str] = {
    "your_jwt_secret_key_here_please_change_in_production",
    "your_jwt_secret_key_here_change_in_production_please_use_a_strong_secret",
    "change-me-in-production",
    "change-me-must-match-platform-deploy-env",
    "minioadmin",
}

def assert_secure_secret(key_name: str, value: str | None) -> None:
    # Dev escape hatch MUST be explicitly named and set
    escape_hatch = os.getenv("ALLOW_INSECURE_SECRETS", "").strip().lower()
    if escape_hatch in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}:
        return

    text = (value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise RuntimeError(f"FATAL SECURITY GUARD: {key_name} is unset or empty. Process halted.")
    
    # Unconditional check: Cannot be bypassed by omitting ENV=prod
    if text in _INSECURE_SENTINELS:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"FATAL SECURITY GUARD: {key_name} contains a known public repository sentinel string. "
            f"Refusing to start. Set a secure, random value or set ALLOW_INSECURE_SECRETS=1 for dev."
        )
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```python

    if config.is_production:

            raise RuntimeError("Insecure secret in production!")
    # In non-production, silent execution proceeds with public sentinel keys
```

**RULE**:
Every execution path inside a `withCheckedContinuation` or `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` block MUST invoke `continuation.resume(...)` exactly once. Any catch block, error propagation branch, or early exit condition that resumes the continuation with an error or value MUST immediately terminate the scope using an explicit `return` or `throw`.

**WHY**:
Swift's concurrency runtime treats resuming a continuation more than once as an invariant violation. In release mode, double resumption leads to fatal memory corruption and immediate process termination (`EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION` or `SIGTRAP: Fatal error: Continuation already resumed`). Resuming zero times leaks the suspended Task indefinitely, creating zombie threads and unbounded memory leaks.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any Swift codebase bridging legacy completion handler APIs, delegate protocols, C callback routines, or POSIX dispatch queues into Modern Swift Concurrency (`async`/`await`).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```swift
func executeProcess() async throws -> ProcessResult {
    try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
        workerQueue.async {
            do {
                let session = try startUnderlyingSession()
                // Invariant: Success path resumes and immediately terminates scope
                continuation.resume(returning: session.result)
                return
            } catch {
                // Invariant: Failure path MUST explicitly return after resume
                continuation.resume(throwing: error)
                return
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```swift
// CRITICAL BUG: Falling through after continuation.resume(throwing:)
func executeProcessBuggy() async throws -> ProcessResult {
    try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
        workerQueue.async {
            do {
                try startUnderlyingSession()
            } catch {
                // Error handled, but missing explicit return!
                continuation.resume(throwing: error)
            }
            // FATAL CRASH: Continuation resumed a second time on error!
            continuation.resume(returning: fallbackResult)
        }
    }
}
```

```swift
    let mock = MockFaultyProvider(shouldFail: true)
    do {
        _ = try await mock.startShell()
        XCTFail("Must throw error")
    } catch {
        XCTAssertEqual(mock.resumeInvocationCount, 1, "Continuation invoked more than once")
    }
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [thebaselab/codeapp](https://github.com/thebaselab/codeapp) (Revision: `8964f069`).

**RULE**:
Before invoking any non-fast-forward checkout or merge operation via `libgit2` or Git wrapper APIs, the client engine MUST evaluate the dirty status of tracked files in the index and working directory. If any tracked file contains uncommitted modifications (`.workTreeModified`, `.workTreeDeleted`, `.indexModified`, etc.), the pull/merge operation MUST abort immediately before mutating HEAD or checking out references.

**WHY**:
Libgit2's `git_checkout_tree` with `.Safe` or `.Force` strategies does not automatically mirror CLI Git’s porcelain pull protection. Invoking merge resolution when the working tree is dirty results in silent truncation, state overwrites, or partial file clobbering, causing irreversible data loss for user edits.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Custom Git GUI clients, embedded IDEs, mobile IDEs, or automated Git agents operating directly on Git indices and working trees via native bindings (`libgit2`, `nodegit`, `SwiftGit2`, `pygit2`).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```swift
public func ensureCleanWorkingTree(repository: Repository) throws {
    let trackedChanges: Diff.Status = [
        .indexNew, .indexModified, .indexDeleted, .indexRenamed, .indexTypeChange,
        .workTreeModified, .workTreeDeleted, .workTreeRenamed, .workTreeTypeChange,
        .conflicted
    ]
    // Empty options exclude untracked files, matching Git's porcelain pull behavior
    let entries = try repository.status(options: []).get()
    let hasDirtyTrackedFiles = entries.contains { entry in
        !entry.status.intersection(trackedChanges).isEmpty
    }
    
    guard !hasDirtyTrackedFiles else {
        throw NSError(
            domain: "org.libgit2.SwiftGit2",
            code: 1,
            userInfo: [
                NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: "Your local changes would be overwritten by pull. Commit or discard them before pulling."
            ]
        )
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```swift
// CRITICAL DATA LOSS: Direct merge without verifying working directory hygiene

    let analysis = try repository.mergeAnalysis(remoteBranch)
    if analysis.contains(.normal) {
        // Will overwrite user uncommitted work tree files without notice!
        try repository.merge(remoteBranch, strategy: [.Safe])
        try repository.checkout(remoteBranch, strategy: [.Force])
    }
}
```

**RULE**:
When caching data derived from dynamic filesystem URIs or file paths, the lookup key MUST be sanitized and canonicalized (decoding percent-escapes, stripping base workspace scheme/prefixes, and normalizing directory separators) PRIOR to querying the cache. The exact normalization transform MUST be applied identically on both Cache Insertion (`set`) and Cache Retrieval (`get`).

**WHY**:
Filesystem APIs and WebView bridges routinely alternate between URL string formats (`file:///var/mobile/...` vs `/var/mobile/...` vs `percent-encoded%20path`). If key canonicalization occurs after a cache query, the lookup key (raw URL) will never match the stored key (relative canonical path), dropping the cache hit rate to 0%. This forces expensive filesystem disk reads, Git OID tree walks, and blob decoding on every keystroke or frame render.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Caches, indexing pipelines, and lookup registries handling filesystem paths, Git diff providers, language servers, or remote resource URLs.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```swift
final class DiffContentCache {
    private let cache = NSCache<NSString, NSString>()
    private let workspaceURL: URL

    init(workspaceURL: URL) {
        self.workspaceURL = workspaceURL
    }

    private func canonicalize(path: String) -> String {
        return path
            .replacingOccurrences(of: workspaceURL.absoluteString, with: "")
            .removingPercentEncoding ?? path
    }

    func content(for rawPath: String, compute: (String) throws -> String) throws -> String {
        // Invariant: Canonicalize BEFORE checking cache
        let canonicalKey = canonicalize(path: rawPath)
        
        if let cached = cache.object(forKey: canonicalKey as NSString) {
            return cached as String
        }

        let computedValue = try compute(canonicalKey)
        cache.setObject(computedValue as NSString, forKey: canonicalKey as NSString)
        return computedValue
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```swift
// FLAWED: Cache lookup with un-normalized rawPath, insertion with normalized path
func content(for rawPath: String) throws -> String {
    // BUG: Raw string tested against normalized cache key -> Guaranteed Miss
    if let cached = cache.object(forKey: rawPath as NSString) {
        return cached as String
    }

    let normalizedKey = rawPath
        .replacingOccurrences(of: self.workspaceURL.absoluteString, with: "")
        .removingPercentEncoding ?? rawPath

    let result = try readBlob(normalizedKey)
    cache.setObject(result as NSString, forKey: normalizedKey as NSString)
    return result
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [projectdiscovery/nuclei](https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei) (Revision: `2e258fc3`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When integrating third-party client libraries into automated scanning engines or high-throughput CLI tools, dialers MUST NOT permit implicit background connection retry loops. `DialerRetries` (or equivalent background reconnect mechanisms) MUST be pinned to `1` (or explicitly disabled), and dialer timeout budgets MUST strictly defer to caller-provided `context.Context` lifecycles. Furthermore, the library's internal logging mechanism MUST be redirected away from raw `os.Stderr` to the application's logging pipeline.

**WHY**:
Third-party clients (such as `go-redis/v9`) frequently implement background reconnection loops with hardcoded retry counts and exponential backoffs (e.g., 5 attempts with 100ms sleeps). When dialing a filtered or closed port, these retry loops spawn detached goroutines that ignore the parent context's cancellation. A scan step with an intended 1-second timeout can block worker pool slots for 25+ seconds. Additionally, unintercepted client errors printed directly to `os.Stderr` pollute structured CLI output (e.g., JSONL streams) and produce false alarms in CI/CD log parsers.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply whenever embedding third-party database drivers, message brokers, caching clients, or network protocol packages (Redis, MongoDB, LDAP, AMQP, gRPC) inside concurrent workers, DAST scanners, or serverless functions where task boundaries are strictly bound to bounded contexts.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```go
package redisclient

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net"
	"time"

	"github.com/projectdiscovery/gologger"
	"github.com/redis/go-redis/v9"
)

// dialAttempts replaces go-redis's default of 5. Background goroutines inside go-redis
// dialer retry loops ignore caller contexts, causing multi-second worker stalls.
const dialAttempts = 1

func init() {
	// Re-route third-party internal logging to prevent direct stderr pollution
	redis.SetLogger(warningLogger{})
}

type warningLogger struct{}
```

> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When serializing unstructured, dynamic configuration maps (such as metadata decoded from YAML) into JSON, the serialization layer MUST recursively walk all collections and transform `map[interface{}]interface{}` (or `map[any]any`) into `map[string]interface{}` (or `map[string]any`). Non-string keys MUST be converted to strings via uniform representation (`fmt.Sprint`), and collisions resulting from stringification MUST be explicitly detected and rejected before encoding. Furthermore, custom `MarshalJSON` implementations on domain models MUST type-alias the receiver (`type alias T`) prior to marshaling to prevent unbounded recursive calls.

**WHY**:
Go's standard `encoding/json` package refuses to serialize maps whose keys are not strings, integers, or types implementing `encoding.TextMarshaler`. Conversely, YAML parsers (e.g., `gopkg.in/yaml.v2` or `yaml.v3`) routinely decode unstructured or dynamically typed dictionaries into `map[interface{}]interface{}`. Directly passing YAML-unmarshaled nested metadata into `json.Marshal` triggers runtime panic or errors (`json: unsupported type: map[interface{}]interface{}`). Additionally, implementing `MarshalJSON` without an intermediate type alias causes recursive calls to the same method, resulting in stack overflow (`runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit`).

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any Go system receiving generic data models via YAML, MessagePack, or BSON that must subsequently be exposed via JSON REST APIs, serialized to JSONL event logs, or forwarded to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```go
package typesafe

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
)

// ToJSONValue walks nested data structures and guarantees that all maps
// have string keys, preventing json.Marshal runtime failures.
func ToJSONValue(value interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
	switch typed := value.(type) {
	case map[interface{}]interface{}:
		converted := make(map[string]interface{}, len(typed))
		for key, item := range typed {
			name := fmt.Sprint(key)
			if _, exists := converted[name]; exists {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("map key %q collides after string conversion", name)
			}
			encoded, err := ToJSONValue(item)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			converted[name] = encoded
		}
		return converted, nil
	case map[string]interface{}:
		return ToJSONMap(typed)
	case []interface{}:
		converted := make([]interface{}, len(typed))
		for i, item := range typed {
			encoded, err := ToJSONValue(item)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			converted[i] = encoded
		}
		return converted, nil
	default:
		return value, nil
	}
}

func ToJSONMap(m map[string]interface{}) (map[string]interface{}, error) {
	if m == nil {
		return nil, nil
	}
	converted := make(map[string]interface{}, len(m))
	for key, item := range m {
		encoded, err := ToJSONValue(item)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		converted[key] = encoded
	}
	return converted, nil
}

type MetadataWrapper struct {
	Name     string                 `json:"name"`
	Metadata map[string]interface{} `json:"metadata"`
}

// MarshalJSON safely serializes dynamic metadata and avoids recursion using a type alias.
func (m MetadataWrapper) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	type metadataWrapper MetadataWrapper // Type alias drops custom MarshalJSON method
	encoded := metadataWrapper(m)

	cleanMeta, err := ToJSONMap(m.Metadata)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	encoded.Metadata = cleanMeta
	return json.Marshal(encoded)
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [projectdiscovery/nuclei](https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei) (Revision: `2e258fc3`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When persisting process configuration, state checkpoints, or resume files across CLI runs, state files MUST be written using the Atomic Tempfile Replace pattern:
1. Write all state bytes to a temporary file located in the *same* filesystem directory as the destination path (`os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(target), ".prefix-*")`).
2. Explicitly set permissions via `tempFile.Chmod(0o600)`.
3. Flush OS disk buffers via `tempFile.Sync()`.
4. Close file descriptor before renaming.
5. Atomically replace target path via `os.Rename`.
6. Defensively execute `defer os.Remove(tempPath)` to prevent orphan tempfiles upon error.

**WHY**:
Directly truncating and overwriting state files (`os.OpenFile(path, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC|os.O_CREATE)`) creates a window of vulnerability where a process crash (SIGINT, SIGKILL, power outage, or OS OOM) leaves behind a 0-byte or corrupted JSON/state file. Writing the tempfile to the system `/tmp` directory instead of the destination directory will cause `os.Rename` to fail across filesystem or mount-point boundaries with `EXDEV` ("invalid cross-device link").

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to all stateful desktop, CLI, or server agents updating on-disk state (e.g., scan progress, authentication tokens, template catalogs, resume metadata).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```go
package atomicfile

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

// WriteStateAtomically enforces crash-consistency, uniform filesystem boundaries,
// and safe sync before directory inode replacement.
func WriteStateAtomically(targetPath string, data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error {
	dir := filepath.Dir(targetPath)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mkdir directory %q: %w", dir, err)
	}

	// Invariant: Tempfile MUST reside in identical directory to guarantee same filesystem partition
	temp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, "."+filepath.Base(targetPath)+"-*")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create tempfile for %q: %w", targetPath, err)
	}
	tempPath := temp.Name()

	// Guarantee cleanup if panic or failure occurs before successful rename
	cleaned := false
	defer func() {
		if !cleaned {
			_ = temp.Close()
			_ = os.Remove(tempPath)
		}
	}()

	if err := temp.Chmod(perm); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("chmod tempfile %q: %w", tempPath, err)
	}

	if _, err := temp.Write(data); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("write tempfile %q: %w", tempPath, err)
	}

	// Flush dirty disk blocks to physical media
	if err := temp.Sync(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("sync tempfile %q: %w", tempPath, err)
	}

	if err := temp.Close(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("close tempfile %q: %w", tempPath, err)
	}

	// Atomic inode replacement on POSIX and modern Windows OS
	if err := os.Rename(tempPath, targetPath); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("replace %q with %q: %w", targetPath, tempPath, err)
	}

	cleaned = true
	return nil
}
```

```go
func TestAtomicWriteFileIntegrity(t *testing.T) {

	target := filepath.Join(dir, "state.json")
	initial := []byte(`{"version":"1.0.0"}`)
	require.NoError(t, WriteStateAtomically(target, initial, 0o600))

	updated := []byte(`{"version":"2.0.0"}`)
	require.NoError(t, WriteStateAtomically(target, updated, 0o600))

	require.NoError(t, err)
```

**RULE**:
When building frameworks that expose internal engine interfaces, schema contracts, or rendering directives via raw SQL column aliases, you MUST NOT map interface semantics to SQL reserved keywords without providing safe, non-reserved architectural aliases and comprehensive multi-dialect escaping.

**WHY**:
Different database engines enforce strict, non-overridable lexer and parser reserved keyword tables. For instance, in Microsoft SQL Server (T-SQL), `CLOSE` is a non-contextual reserved keyword (used to terminate cursors via `CLOSE cursor_name`). A query such as `SELECT 'modal' AS component, 'Dismiss' AS close;` immediately raises a fatal T-SQL syntax error (`Msg 156, Level 15: Incorrect syntax near the keyword 'close'`). Forcing users to rely on dialect-specific quoting (e.g., `[close]` for MSSQL, `"close"` for Postgres, `` `close` `` for MySQL) breaks cross-database query portability—a fundamental value proposition of unified data engines.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Applies to all database abstraction layers, query generators, meta-programming database tools, and template engines where SQL column aliases act as parameter keys.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
Implement dual-alias resolution in both metadata catalogs and template macro expressions, favoring reserved-word-free synonyms while falling back safely:

```handlebars

<div class="modal-header">
    <h5 class="modal-title" id="{{id}}-title">{{title}}</h5>
    <button type="button" 
            class="btn-close" 
            data-bs-dismiss="modal" 
            aria-label="{{default (default close_label close) "close"}}">
    </button>
</div>
<div class="modal-footer">
    {{#if (or close_label close)}}
        <button type="button" class="btn me-primary" data-bs-dismiss="modal">
            {{default close_label close}}
        </button>
    {{/if}}
</div>
```

```sql
VALUES
    ('modal', 'close', 'The text to display in the Close button.', 'TEXT', TRUE, TRUE),
    ('modal', 'close_label', 'The same as `close`. Use it on databases where `close` is a reserved word, such as SQL Server.', 'TEXT', TRUE, TRUE);
```

**RULE**:
When generating absolute callback URLs, redirects, or cryptographic authentication identifiers (e.g., OpenID Connect `redirect_uri`) behind reverse proxies, you MUST resolve the transport scheme and hostname from verified `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, and `X-Forwarded-Port` headers rather than the local TCP/TLS socket context, unless explicitly disabled by an untrusted network barrier configuration.

**WHY**:
In modern containerized deployments, applications run inside internal virtual networks bound to unencrypted HTTP sockets (e.g., `http://10.0.0.5:8080` or `http://localhost:9191`) behind edge ingress controllers (Caddy, Traefik, NGINX, AWS ALB) that terminate TLS (`https://app.domain.com:443`). If an application queries its local incoming socket to determine the protocol scheme, it generates `http://...` URIs. When negotiating OIDC authorization code grants, the identity provider matches the client's `redirect_uri` byte-for-byte against registered URIs. Emitting `http://app.domain.com/callback` instead of `https://app.domain.com/callback` causes an immediate, unrecoverable authorization rejection (`redirect_uri_mismatch`).

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Applies to all HTTP application servers, web frameworks, auth middleware, and proxy-aware edge services generating absolute URIs.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
Implement an RFC 7239 / de-facto header resolution hierarchy on the incoming request context:

```rust
use actix_web::HttpRequest;

pub struct RequestUrlResolver<'a> {
    req: &'a HttpRequest,
    trust_forwarded_headers: bool,
}

impl<'a> RequestUrlResolver<'a> {
    pub fn new(req: &'a HttpRequest, trust_forwarded_headers: bool) -> Self {
        Self { req, trust_forwarded_headers }
    }

    /// Resolves the canonical public-facing scheme (https or http)
    pub fn scheme(&self) -> &str {
        if self.trust_forwarded_headers {
            if let Some(proto) = self.req.headers().get("X-Forwarded-Proto") {
                if let Ok(proto_str) = proto.to_str() {
                    // Extract first hop if multiple proxies are chained: "https, http"
                    return proto_str.split(',').next().unwrap_or("https").trim();
                }
            }
        }
        self.req.connection_info().scheme()
    }

    /// Resolves canonical public host with port awareness
    pub fn host(&self) -> &str {
        if self.trust_forwarded_headers {
            if let Some(host) = self.req.headers().get("X-Forwarded-Host") {
                if let Ok(host_str) = host.to_str() {
                    return host_str.split(',').next().unwrap_or("localhost").trim();
                }
            }
        }
        self.req.connection_info().host()
    }

    /// Assembles an absolute URL guaranteed to match public reverse proxy termination
    pub fn construct_absolute_url(&self, path: &str) -> String {
        let scheme = self.scheme();
        let host = self.host();
        let normalized_path = if path.starts_with('/') { path } else { &format!("/{path}") };
        format!("{scheme}://{host}{normalized_path}")
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:

> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
A web engine executing multi-statement streaming pipelines MUST NOT emit an HTTP 200 OK status header before statement execution begins, and MUST halt error serialization to the client if execution fails while in the header processing state.

**WHY**:
Once the HTTP response status line (`HTTP/1.1 200 OK`) and response headers are flushed over the socket, the HTTP status is immutable. If a database query fails *after* headers are sent, the server can only abort the TCP stream or write an inline error box inside the 200 OK HTML payload. This leads to two critical vulnerabilities:
1. **Security/Information Leak**: Emitting raw database backtraces or SQL syntax errors into the response body of a 200 OK response can leak database structure, table names, and query parameters to unauthenticated callers.
2. **Client-Side Semantic Failure**: Automated callers, webhooks, and reverse proxies assume a successful transaction because of the 200 OK status code, leading to silent data-loss states where failed insertions are treated as successful.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Applies to all HTTP engines, database-to-HTTP gateways, and streaming template renderers.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
Implement a two-phase state machine that segregates the header collection phase from body chunking, intercepting errors before any socket write occurs:

```rust
pub async fn handle_error(self, err: anyhow::Error) -> anyhow::Result<PageContext> {
    // 1. Convert the error into a sanitized, client-safe error representation
    let client_error = ClientError::new(&err, self.app_state.config.environment, None);
    
    // 2. In production mode (where is_generic() returns true), NEVER start a 200 body
    if client_error.is_generic() {
        // Bubble up error so Actix-Web's top-level error middleware generates 
        // an authentic HTTP 500 Internal Server Error response without leaking details
        return Err(err);
    }
    
    // 3. In development mode: developer debugging experience is prioritized;
    // render the error component directly into the body for immediate visual feedback
    log::debug!("Handling header error in development mode: {err}");
    let mut data = client_error.to_html_data();
    data["component"] = json!("error");
    self.start_body(data).await
}
```

```rust
    // Flushes HTTP 200 OK directly to wire
    writer.send_status(StatusCode::OK).await?;
    
    // Any database failure here now happens AFTER 200 OK was sent!
    let rows = db.fetch_all("SELECT * FROM invalid_table").await;
    match rows {
        Ok(r) => writer.write_body(r).await?,
        Err(e) => {
            // DISASTER: 200 OK is already received by client!
            // Writes stack trace into a "successful" response.
            writer.write_body(format!("<div>Error: {e}</div>")).await?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [rainbow-me/rainbow](https://github.com/rainbow-me/rainbow) (Revision: `11a07420`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
Financial number formatters that scale across varying magnitudes (sub-cent, whole units, compact suffix notation) MUST determine threshold tier eligibility using the intermediate value rounded for that specific tier, BUT MUST evaluate the formatted digits exactly once against the unrounded raw float/BigInt magnitude. Display systems MUST NOT evaluate tier boundary thresholds on unrounded floats while simultaneously rendering rounded numbers, and MUST NOT format percentages or token values with non-deterministic variable trailing zeros adjacent to fixed-precision fields.

**WHY**:
Evaluating magnitude tiers on raw values causes catastrophic UI off-by-one boundary glitching. For example, `$99,999.60` evaluated raw against a `$100K` threshold would select whole-dollar formatting and round up to `$100,000`, while `$100,000.40` would select compact formatting and display as `$100.0K`. Furthermore, double-rounding (rounding to 2 decimal places, then scaling, then rounding to 1 decimal place) causes drift: `$999,949.50` would double-round to `$1,000.0K` (`$1.0M`) instead of staying strictly at `$999.9K`.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to any frontend display system, financial dashboard, P&L calculator, or analytics interface converting high-precision arbitrary numbers into compact localized strings (`K`, `M`, `B`, `T`).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
import {
  divWorklet,
  greaterThanOrEqualToWorklet,
  lessThanWorklet,
  toFixedWorklet,
  equalWorklet,
} from '@/framework/core/safeMath';
import { addCommasToNumber } from '@/framework/ui/utils/addCommasToNumber';

const SUFFIXES = [
  { suffix: 'K', value: 1e3 },
  { suffix: 'M', value: 1e6 },
  { suffix: 'B', value: 1e9 },
  { suffix: 'T', value: 1e12 },
] as const;

const COMPACT_AMOUNT_FROM = 100_000;
const COMPACT_PERCENTAGE_FROM = 1_000;

/**
 * Abbreviates an arbitrary precision magnitude string into fixed 1-decimal compact notation.
 * Preserves trailing zeros (e.g., "184.0K") and increments tier dynamically if rounding pushes >= 1000.
 */
export function abbreviate(magnitude: string): string {
  'worklet';
  let tier = 0;
  let scaled = toFixedWorklet(divWorklet(magnitude, SUFFIXES[tier].value), 1);
  
  // Loop guard: advance tier if rounding rolls value over to 1000.0
  while (tier < SUFFIXES.length - 1 && greaterThanOrEqualToWorklet(scaled, 1000)) {
    tier += 1;
    scaled = toFixedWorklet(divWorklet(magnitude, SUFFIXES[tier].value), 1);
  }
  return `${addCommasToNumber(scaled)}${SUFFIXES[tier].suffix}`;
}

export function formatPnlPercentage(percentage: string): string {
  'worklet';
  const magnitude = percentage.replace('-', '');
  if (equalWorklet(magnitude, 0)) return '0%';
  
  // Strict rule: <1% decided strictly on raw magnitude before any rounding
  if (lessThanWorklet(magnitude, 1)) return '<1%';
  
  // Evaluate tier boundary against whole units
  const whole = toFixedWorklet(magnitude, 0);
  return `${lessThanWorklet(whole, COMPACT_PERCENTAGE_FROM) ? whole : abbreviate(magnitude)}%`;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Selecting compact notation using unrounded raw value,
// and trimming trailing zeros inconsistently via standard parseFloat/toFixed.
export function badFormat(amount: number): string {
  // Bug 1: 99999.6 is < 100000, so it outputs "$100000" instead of jumping to "$100.0K"
  if (amount < 100000) {
    return `$${Math.round(amount)}`;
  }
  // Bug 2: 999950 / 1e6 = 0.99995 -> toFixed(1) = "1.0", but parseFloat drops the zero -> "1M"
  // resulting in misaligned tables where "$184K" sits next to "$166.5K"
  const scaled = amount / 1000;
  return `$${parseFloat(scaled.toFixed(1))}K`;
}
```

```typescript
  { amount: '999950', expected: '$1.0M' },
  { amount: '0.9949', expected: '$0.99' },
```

**RULE**:
When an entity's domain eligibility (e.g., P&L tracking, Holder rankings) depends on dynamic asynchronous metadata (e.g., asset classification), that eligibility state MUST be derived inside a centralized, singleton reactive store with locked dependencies (`lockDependencies: true`) and strict equality guarantees (`shallowEqual`). Downstream UI components and data queries MUST NOT independently execute metadata requests or maintain bespoke boolean gates. Furthermore, metadata fetches MUST read directly from existing parent cache entries (`queryClient.getQueryData`) before invoking network fallbacks.

**WHY**:
Distributing eligibility checks across multiple UI components creates race conditions where a fast UI transition (e.g., switching the active token) causes an downstream store to pair the newly selected token's address with the *previous* token's cached classification type. This emits invalid API queries (e.g., sending Codex requests for stablecoins or native gas assets), creates flickering UI states, wastes mobile bandwidth, and risks downstream backend rate-limiting.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Applies to any state architecture where multiple distinct visualizations or query engines rely on a secondary asynchronous attribute of a primary selected domain entity.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
import { createDerivedStore, createQueryStore, shallowEqual } from '@storesjs/stores';
import { queryClient } from '@/react-query/queryClient';

// 1. Parameterized store with decoupled shallow caching
const useViewedTokenTypeStore = createQueryStore<string | null, ViewedTokenTypeParams>({
  fetcher: fetchViewedTokenType,
  params: {
    token: $ => $(useChartsStore, ({ token }) => 
      token && !isNativeAsset(token.address, token.chainId)
        ? { address: token.address, chainId: token.chainId }
        : null, 
      shallowEqual
    ),
    currency: $ => $(userAssetsStoreManager, state => state.currency),
  },
  staleTime: 3600000,
});

async function fetchViewedTokenType({ token, currency }: ViewedTokenTypeParams): Promise<string | null> {
  if (!token) return null;
  const queryKey = externalTokenQueryKey({ address: token.address, chainId: token.chainId, currency });
  
  // Cache piggybacking: Never fetch if chart parent has already fetched or cached the entity
  const cached = queryClient.getQueryData<ExternalTokenResult>(queryKey);
  if (cached) return cached.type ?? null;
  
  const fresh = await queryClient.fetchQuery(queryKey, externalTokenQueryFunction, {
    staleTime: 3600000,
  });
  return fresh?.type ?? null;
}

// 2. Atomic, centralized eligibility derivation with locked dependency transitions
export const usePnlEligibleToken = createDerivedStore(
  $ => {
    const token = $(useChartsStore, state => state.token);
    const type = $(useViewedTokenTypeStore, state => state.getData());

    // Deterministic atomic exclusion: prevents tearing or race pairing
    if (!token || !type || type === 'stablecoin' || type === 'native') {
      return null;
    }
    return {
      address: token.address,
      chainId: token.chainId,
      codexTokenId: `${token.address}:${token.chainId}`,
    };
  },
  { equalityFn: shallowEqual, lockDependencies: true }
);
```

**RULE**:
When implementing design system specifications where typography has been configured with cap-height and baseline font trimming (`includeFontPadding: false` on Android, or explicit line-box leading removal), UI layouts MUST NOT apply raw Figma layout gaps directly. Engineers MUST adjust container margins and layout gaps by adding the delta of the stripped top/bottom font leadings ($$\Delta = \text{Leading}_{\text{untrimmed}} - \text{Leading}_{\text{trimmed}}$$) to reproduce the exact visual rhythm intended by the design spec.

**WHY**:
Design tools like Figma measure vertical auto-layout padding between untrimmed typographic bounding boxes (including font ascender/descender margins). When a production mobile design system strips these paddings to achieve precise geometric alignment with icons and borders, using Figma's nominal values will draw elements noticeably closer together than intended.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [tailscale/tailscale](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale) (Revision: `5a05ac11`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When wrapping an existing or duplicated OS file descriptor (such as a PTY master, socket, or pipe) with runtime-managed I/O wrappers (`os.NewFile` in Go, or an asynchronous event loop registrar in Rust/C++), the descriptor MUST be configured with non-blocking mode (`O_NONBLOCK`) and close-on-exec (`FD_CLOEXEC`) BEFORE runtime registration, and all metadata operations (such as `ioctl` or flag queries) MUST be executed using non-releasing raw syscall barriers (`syscall.RawConn.Control`). A runtime-wrapped file's descriptor MUST NOT be queried using bare accessor methods (such as `File.Fd()`).

**WHY**:
In Go and similar runtimes, calling `File.Fd()` automatically places the underlying descriptor back into blocking mode so external syscalls can use it. This strips `O_NONBLOCK`, disconnecting the descriptor from the runtime network poller (`epoll`/`kqueue`). When another thread concurrently invokes `File.Close()`, the pending I/O thread remains blocked in a kernel-level read/write wait that cannot be interrupted, causing deadlocks, wedged shutdown hooks, and connection leaks. Furthermore, uncoordinated closes can release an integer descriptor that is immediately recycled by another goroutine, leading to destructive `EBADF` or silent corruption of arbitrary resources.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply when bridging low-level POSIX OS primitives (pseudo-terminals, unix domain sockets, SCM_RIGHTS file passing) into runtime-polled abstractions across Go, Rust (Tokio/Mio), and C++ (libuv/Asio).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```go
// Production-grade descriptor duplication and runtime poller binding
func dupPTYMaster(f *os.File) (*os.File, error) {
	raw, err := f.SyscallConn()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("retrieving SyscallConn: %w", err)
	}

	fd := -1
	var dupErr error
	// Control prevents concurrent Close from releasing the fd during invocation
	if err := raw.Control(func(src uintptr) {
		// 1. Atomically allocate lowest available descriptor >= 0 with CLOEXEC
		fd, dupErr = unix.FcntlInt(src, unix.F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, 0)
		if dupErr == nil {
			// 2. Set O_NONBLOCK BEFORE runtime poller ingestion
			dupErr = unix.SetNonblock(fd, true)
		}
	}); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("control invocation failed: %w", err)
	}

	if dupErr != nil {
		if fd != -1 {
			_ = unix.Close(fd)
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("duplicating descriptor: %w", dupErr)
	}

	// 3. Register with Go's runtime poller
	dup := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), f.Name())

	// 4. Invariant Assertion: Verify descriptor is actively managed by runtime poller
	if err := dup.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{}); err != nil {
		_ = dup.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("PTY master descriptor rejected by runtime poller: %w", err)
	}
	return dup, nil
}

// Window resize ioctl synchronized via RawConn
func updateWindowSize(f *os.File, ws *unix.Winsize) error {
	raw, err := f.SyscallConn()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var ioctlErr error
	// raw.Control retains descriptor lock, guaranteeing fd is not closed or reused concurrently
	err = raw.Control(func(fd uintptr) {
		for {
			ioctlErr = unix.IoctlSetWinsize(int(fd), syscall.TIOCSWINSZ, ws)
			if !errors.Is(ioctlErr, unix.EINTR) {
				break
			}
		}
	})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return ioctlErr
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```go
// NEVER extract bare Fd() and mutate flags on managed abstractions

	// BUG: Calling f.Fd() sets the underlying descriptor back to BLOCKING mode in Go!
	srcFd := f.Fd() 

	// BUG: Raw dup leaves FD_CLOEXEC unset; leaks descriptors into child processes
	newFd, err := unix.Dup(int(srcFd))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	newFile := os.NewFile(uintptr(newFd), f.Name())
	// BUG: External ioctl via raw newFd will race with concurrent newFile.Close()
	// and cause undefined behavior or write to a recycled descriptor.
	return newFile, nil
}
```

```go
func AssertDescriptorPollable(t *testing.T, f *os.File) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := f.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(-1 * time.Second)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("file %s is not integrated with Go runtime network poller: %v", f.Name(), err)
	}
	var b [1]byte
	_, err := f.Read(b[:])
	if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrDeadlineExceeded) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrDeadlineExceeded on expired deadline, got: %v", err)
	}
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [tailscale/tailscale](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale) (Revision: `5a05ac11`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
DNS client and proxy engines that evaluate enterprise routing policies MUST distinguish between configured authoritative routes and ambient/unconfigured fallback resolvers. When resolving a query under a configured split domain, search domain, or explicit DNS override, if an authoritative denial (`NXDOMAIN`) or server failure (`SERVFAIL`) is returned by the designated resolver, the engine MUST NOT fall back to local host resolvers or ambient cloud-host metadata resolvers (`169.254.169.254`).

**WHY**:
Falling back to host resolvers when an internal or policy-designated resolver returns an error breaks zero-trust split-horizon DNS models. It allows private namespace queries (such as `database.internal.corp`) to leak out to public/ISP resolvers or cloud-provider ambient forwarders, exposing internal architecture. Additionally, it causes non-deterministic query resolution where down services resolve to public sinkholes, causing severe security and routing violations.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to all DNS forwarders, internal resolvers, HTTP clients, and connection dialers in VPN software, service meshes, or enterprise routing daemons.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```go
type DNSForwardRoute struct {
	Suffix    string
	Resolvers []string
	Ambient   bool // true if derived from host environment/DHCP/cloud metadata
}

type ResolverEngine struct {
	mu     sync.RWMutex
	routes []DNSForwardRoute
}

func (r *ResolverEngine) HasConfiguredRouteFor(name string) bool {
	r.mu.RLock()
	defer r.mu.RUnlock()
	for _, route := range r.routes {
		if route.Ambient {
			// Ambient fallbacks MUST NOT prevent strict resolution failures
			continue
		}
		if route.Suffix == "." || strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(name), strings.ToLower(route.Suffix)) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (r *ResolverEngine) Resolve(ctx context.Context, name string) ([]netip.Addr, error) {
	hasRoute := r.HasConfiguredRouteFor(name)

	ips, err := r.queryTailnetUpstream(ctx, name)
	if err == nil && len(ips) > 0 {
		return ips, nil
	}

	// CRITICAL INVARIANT: Never fall back to host resolver if the name belongs to a configured route
	if hasRoute {
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("upstream resolution failed for configured route %q: %w", name, err)
		}
		return nil, &net.DNSError{Err: "no such host", Name: name, IsNotFound: true}
	}

	// Only unconfigured queries may fall back to host resolver / ambient forwarders
	return r.queryHostFallback(ctx, name)
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```go

	ips, err := r.queryTailnetUpstream(ctx, name)
	// ANTI-PATTERN: Blindly falling back to host resolution leaks corporate namespaces
	if err != nil || len(ips) == 0 {
		return r.queryHostFallback(ctx, name) 
	}
	return ips, nil
}
```

```go
	harness := setupDNSHarness(t)
	harness.AddSplitRoute("corp.internal.", mockBrokenResolver) // returns SERVFAIL
	harness.SetHostFallback(mockHostResolver)                   // must not be called

	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected error, got successful resolution")
	}
```

> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
Stream parsers, terminal emulators, and character decoders reading from network chunks or file descriptors MUST NOT attempt to decode or stringify arbitrary sub-slices of raw byte buffers directly into unicode/UTF-8 strings without buffering trailing incomplete UTF-8 codepoint sequences across read boundaries.

**WHY**:
UTF-8 codepoints span between 1 and 4 bytes. When network chunking or OS pipe read boundaries bifurcate a multi-byte sequence (for example, split an em-dash `\xE2\x94\x80` between index 4095 and 0), treating each chunk as an isolated string replaces the split boundary bytes with Unicode Replacement Characters (`\uFFFD`, ``). This permanently corrupts TUI terminal layouts (such as `htop`/`tmux`), corrupts cryptographic base64/hex tokens, and can invalidate structured data payloads.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any stream processor, WebAssembly JS-bridge writer, terminal pipeline, or log streaming engine reading arbitrary byte buffers and transforming them into high-level strings.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
export class UTF-8ChunkResynchronizer {
  private pending: Uint8Array = new Uint8Array(0)
  private readonly decoder = new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: false })

  public push(chunk: Uint8Array): string {
    // 1. Prepend remaining partial sequence from prior read
    let buf: Uint8Array
    if (this.pending.length > 0) {
      buf = new Uint8Array(this.pending.length + chunk.length)
      buf.set(this.pending, 0)
      buf.set(chunk, this.pending.length)
      this.pending = new Uint8Array(0)
    } else {
      buf = chunk
    }

    if (buf.length === 0) {
      return ""
    }

    // 2. Scan backwards from the tail to identify incomplete UTF-8 leading bytes
    const len = buf.length
    let incompleteIndex = -1

    for (let i = len - 1; i >= 0 && i >= len - 4; i--) {
      const byte = buf[i]
      // ASCII single byte (0xxxxxxx)
      if ((byte & 0x80) === 0) {
        break
      }
      // Continuation byte (10xxxxxx)
      if ((byte & 0xc0) === 0x80) {
        continue
      }
      // Leading bytes:
      let expectedBytes = 0
      if ((byte & 0xe0) === 0xc0) expectedBytes = 2      // 110xxxxx
      else if ((byte & 0xf0) === 0xe0) expectedBytes = 3 // 1110xxxx
      else if ((byte & 0xf8) === 0xf0) expectedBytes = 4 // 11110xxx

      const availableBytes = len - i
      if (availableBytes < expectedBytes) {
        incompleteIndex = i
      }
      break
    }

    // 3. Stash partial byte tail for next read pass
    let validSlice: Uint8Array
    if (incompleteIndex !== -1) {
      this.pending = buf.slice(incompleteIndex)
      validSlice = buf.slice(0, incompleteIndex)
    } else {
      validSlice = buf
    }

    return this.decoder.decode(validSlice)
  }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// NEVER stringify raw network chunks directly without stateful byte accumulation
class BadTermWriter {
  public write(chunk: Uint8Array): void {
    // BUG: If chunk cuts off an 0xE2 0x94 multi-byte rune mid-stream,
    // String.fromCharCode or standard TextDecoder emits  and loses data!
    const text = new TextDecoder().decode(chunk)
    window.term.write(text)
  }
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Implement property tests verifying zero corruption over variable buffer sliding windows spanning 1 to 8 bytes across multi-byte Unicode strings:
```typescript
describe("UTF8ChunkResynchronizer", () => {
  it("preserves continuous unicode strings across boundary cuts", () => {
    const resync = new UTF8ChunkResynchronizer()
    const input = "─".repeat(5000) // 3-byte character: \xE2\x94\x80
    const rawBytes = new TextEncoder().encode(input)
    
    let output = ""
    // Slice across an irregular buffer boundary prime size (e.g. 7 bytes)
    const chunkSize = 7
    for (let i = 0; i < rawBytes.length; i += chunkSize) {
      const slice = rawBytes.slice(i, i + chunkSize)
      output += resync.push(slice)
    }
    expect(output.includes("\uFFFD")).toBe(false)
    expect(output).toEqual(input)
  })
})
```

PROVENANCE_END -->
> **Provenance**: Harvested from [citusdata/citus](https://github.com/citusdata/citus) (Revision: `843ef6f0`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When issuing asynchronous control signals (e.g., `SIGINT`, `kill()`, abort RPCs) to process slots or backends based on distributed state inspection, the caller MUST verify both the **globally scoped node identifier** and the **locally unique monotonically increasing transaction counter** under an atomic spinlock immediately prior to signal emission. A signal MUST NOT be emitted if either identifier has diverged or if the target backend has transitioned out of the resolved transaction.

**WHY**:
In distributed architectures, monotonic counters (such as transaction IDs or query IDs) are initialized locally per node. Without validating the origin node ID along with the sequence counter under lock, cross-node sequence collisions cause the coordinator to misidentify a locally initiated transaction as a remote foreign transaction with the same numeric sequence. Furthermore, during the time elapsed between deadlock detection graph traversal and process signaling (a TOCTOU race window), the backend can commit or abort the deadlocked transaction and start an unrelated query. Checking only that `transactionNumber != 0` results in signaling an innocent transaction.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply in any distributed orchestration layer, clustered database, or distributed deadlock detector where an asynchronous supervisory daemon inspects remote process graphs and resolves conflicts by sending OS signals or cancellation frames to worker backend slots.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```c
/*
 * Atomically verifies node origin and transaction sequence counter
 * under a spinlock before signaling the OS process.
 */
bool
SafeCancelDistributedTransaction(PGPROC *proc, const DistributedTransactionId *expectedXactId)
{
    bool cancelled = false;
    BackendData *backendData = &backendManagementShmemData->backends[getProcNo_compat(proc)];

    if (!backendData)
    {
        return false;
    }

    /* Acquire low-level spinlock to prevent TOCTOU state transition */
    SpinLockAcquire(&backendData->mutex);

    DistributedTransactionId *liveXactId = &backendData->transactionId;

    /*
     * Both the monotonic sequence number AND the initiating node identifier
     * MUST match identically. Timestamp is omitted only if sequence numbers
     * are strictly monotonic per node instance.
     */
    if (liveXactId->transactionNumber == expectedXactId->transactionNumber &&
        liveXactId->initiatorNodeIdentifier == expectedXactId->initiatorNodeIdentifier)
    {
        backendData->cancelledDueToDeadlock = true;
        SpinLockRelease(&backendData->mutex);

        /* Signal process immediately after state transition is marked */
        if (SendProcSignal(proc->pid, PROCSIG_RECOVERY_CONFLICT_STARTUP, proc->backendId) < 0)
        {
            ereport(WARNING,
                    (errmsg("Could not signal process %d for distributed cancellation",
                            proc->pid)));
        }
        cancelled = true;
    }
    else
    {
        /* Target backend changed transactions or originated from a different node */
        SpinLockRelease(&backendData->mutex);
    }

    return cancelled;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```c
// ANTI-PATTERN: Verifying only local transaction non-zero status
// Vulnerable to cross-node counter collisions and TOCTOU signal misdirection.
void
UnsafeCancelDistributedTransaction(PGPROC *proc)
{
    BackendData *backendData = &backendManagementShmemData->backends[getProcNo_compat(proc)];
    
    SpinLockAcquire(&backendData->mutex);
    // BUG: If transaction 42 committed and backend started transaction 43,
    // or if transaction 42 was on node B while local backend was running local txn 42,
    // this cancels an innocent query.
    if (backendData->transactionId.transactionNumber != 0)
    {
        backendData->cancelledDueToDeadlock = true;
        SpinLockRelease(&backendData->mutex);
        kill(proc->pid, SIGINT);
    }
    else
    {
        SpinLockRelease(&backendData->mutex);
    }
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Run multi-session isolation tests where an unrelated local session is forced to stall on a lock, while a separate session injects an external distributed transaction ID with an identical sequence number from node 9999. Invoke `check_distributed_deadlocks()`. Assert via query logs that the foreign deadlocked session receives the cancellation error while the local collision session completes and commits without error (`src/test/regress/spec/isolation_deadlock_detection_txn_number_collision.spec`).

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [citusdata/citus](https://github.com/citusdata/citus) (Revision: `843ef6f0`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When implementing logical replication decoders or change-data-capture (CDC) translators, modified or synthesized tuples MUST NOT overwrite pointers within `ReorderBufferChange` structs (`change->data.tp.newtuple` / `oldtuple`) using memory allocated from transient caller contexts (`CurrentMemoryContext`). Decoded tuple references MUST either be allocated directly inside the reorder buffer’s dedicated tuple slab memory context (`rb->context`) or copied back before reorder buffer release routines are invoked.

**WHY**:
PostgreSQL's logical decoding pipeline allocates change representations inside dedicated `ReorderBuffer` slab allocators. During cleanup (`ReorderBufferFreeChange` -> `ReorderBufferCleanupTXN`), the engine calls `SlabFree()` or `pfree()` on `newtuple` and `oldtuple` expecting headers and chunk markers managed by its internal slab allocator. Overwriting these pointers with tuples allocated via `heap_form_tuple()` in a transient execution context causes `SlabFree` to interpret arbitrary heap data as slab block headers, resulting in memory corruption, invalid pointer dereferences, and fatal walsender `SIGSEGV` aborts.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Applies to database storage engines, replication plugins, logical decoding output plugins, and CDC systems where change records generated by a core transaction engine are intercepted, rewritten, or schema-translated before streaming downstream.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```c
/*
 * Safe translation of tuples in logical replication pipeline.
 * Allocates substitute tuple memory directly from the ReorderBuffer tuple context.
 */
void
TranslateLogicalReorderBufferChange(ReorderBuffer *rb,
                                    ReorderBufferChange *change,
                                    Relation targetRelation)
{
    if (!change->data.tp.newtuple)
    {
        return;
    }

    MemoryContext oldContext = MemoryContextSwitchTo(ReorderBufferGetTupleBufContext(rb));

    HeapTuple originalTuple = &change->data.tp.newtuple->tuple;
    HeapTuple translatedTuple = TranslateHeapTupleSchema(originalTuple, targetRelation);

    /* Allocate custom buffer wrapper from the ReorderBuffer context */
    ReorderBufferTupleBuf *newTupleBuf = ReorderBufferGetTupleBuf(rb, translatedTuple->t_len);
    memcpy(&newTupleBuf->tuple, translatedTuple, HEAPTUPLESIZE);
    memcpy(newTupleBuf->tuple.t_data, translatedTuple->t_data, translatedTuple->t_len);

    /* Free original tuple buffer via reorder buffer slab API */
    ReorderBufferReturnTupleBuf(rb, change->data.tp.newtuple);

    /* Safely assign the reorder-buffer-managed replacement pointer */
    change->data.tp.newtuple = newTupleBuf;

    MemoryContextSwitchTo(oldContext);
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```c
// ANTI-PATTERN: Allocating in transient CurrentMemoryContext and mutating pointers.
void
UnsafeTranslateLogicalChange(ReorderBufferChange *change, TupleDesc newDesc)
{
    // Allocated in CurrentMemoryContext (e.g., MessageContext, ExprContext)
    HeapTuple translated = heap_form_tuple(newDesc, values, isnull);

    // CRITICAL BUG: change->data.tp.newtuple was allocated in rb->context slab.
    // Overwriting it with a heap-allocated pointer causes ReorderBufferFreeChange()
    // to call SlabFree() on a regular palloc chunk, causing SIGSEGV in walsender.
    change->data.tp.newtuple = (ReorderBufferTupleBuf *) translated;
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Execute an end-to-end logical decoding replication test combining DDL schema changes (`DROP COLUMN`), distributed logical shard migration (`force_logical`), and bulk DML updates under AddressSanitizer (ASan) or Valgrind. Assert that `ReorderBufferCleanupTXN` executes cleanly without slab assertion errors or signal 11 traps.
